item.title: Cardinals bid farewell to Nationals, Busch Stadium for 2026
item.description: The visiting Washington Nationals will look to complete a three-game sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The visiting Washington Nationals will look to complete a three-game sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. It will be the final home game of the season for the Cardinals, who are 37-43 at Busch Stadium. On Saturday, the Nationals scored four runs in the top of the 11th inning and held on for an 8-5 win. Washington (73-82) has won six of its past seven games, and a victory Sunday would give the team a .500 mark in September (8-8) despite a recent seven-game losing streak. The Cardinals (75-80), meanwhile, have lost four games in a row. After Sunday's game, they will finish the season at Pittsburgh and Milwaukee. Both St. Louis and Washington sit fourth in their respective divisions with seven games remaining, and both have been eliminated from postseason contention. The Nationals will start right-hander Jake Irvin (2-9, 5.51 ERA) on Sunday, and the Cardinals will counter with rookie left-hander Quinn Mathews (2-3, 3.62). Irvin has struggled since returning from the injured list in late July, going 0-5 with a 5.84 ERA in nine games (eight starts). Last time out, he followed an opener for the first time in his four-year career and gave up three runs on two hits and four walks over five innings against the Los Angeles Angels on Sept. 12. He struck out six and didn't figure into the decision of a 6-5 loss in 10 innings. Irvin has allowed 16 first-inning runs in 19 starts this season. Mathews will make his eighth major league start. Over his past four starts, he is 2-1 with a 1.93 ERA. In his most recent game, he allowed one run on four hits over 6 2/3 innings of a 2-1 win Monday against the San Francisco Giants. He struck out a career-high eight batters and walked two. He retired the first 10 batters he faced and did not allow a hit until the sixth. "(Catcher Leo Bernal) kind of navigated the first three innings -- I think I shook one pitch in three innings, which is unbelievable, to be honest with you," Mathews said. "So a lot of credit to Bernal there, getting me through the first three when I wasn't as sharp as I would have liked to have been." Saturday night, the Nationals won despite blowing their 40th and 41st save chances of the season, losing a 3-2 lead in the ninth and a 4-3 lead in the 10th. Jose Tena had the big hit in the 11th, a two-run double, and the bullpen held on, with Will Dion getting the final out for his first major league save. Washington's Jorbit Vivas had four hits, and Daylen Lile smacked a two-run homer. Jose Fermin and Ivan Herrera had three hits each for St. Louis. The Cardinals pulled to 8-5 and loaded the bases with no outs in the bottom of the 11th, but Nationals relievers retired three hitters in a row -- two by strikeout -- to end the game. For the game, St. Louis was called for a catcher's interference, committed two errors and left 13 men on base. "They've done a really nice job of playing some pretty clean baseball," manager Oliver Marmol said of his team, "and even when we don't, you have the winning run up to the plate in extra innings. There's parts of that game that are highly frustrating." --Field Level Media

item.title: Rangers look for length from Jacob deGrom in finale vs. Jays
item.description: The Texas Rangers have had to turn to their bullpen more often than they would have liked in the first two contests of their three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays in Arlington, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Texas Rangers have had to turn to their bullpen more often than they would have liked in the first two contests of their three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays in Arlington, Texas. After pulling starter Kumar Rocker in the fifth inning of Friday's 7-1 win, Texas manager Skip Schumaker was forced to go to his bullpen with one out in the second on Saturday after starter Cal Quantrill exited the game with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery stepped in and held Toronto hitless over 3 2/3 innings in a 6-2 victory. Schumaker hopes to give his relievers a breather when Jacob deGrom takes the mound in the finale against the Blue Jays on Sunday afternoon. "That's what this team is all about right now," Schumaker said. "... Monty was fantastic. But again, these are team wins, and it's also because of what happened the day before, really covering us today." The veteran deGrom (11-9, 3.79 ERA) has been strong at home this season. The right-hander has a 2.53 ERA with 111 strikeouts in 85 1/3 innings over 15 starts at Globe Life Field. He's coming off an outing in which he allowed just two runs on three hits in five innings against the Boston Red Sox on Sept. 15. He has only made three starts against the Blue Jays in his career, going 1-1 with a 1.65 ERA. The Rangers (78-77) are eyeing a third straight win and a seventh in eight games. Saturday's victory combined with the Houston Astros' loss to the Atlanta Braves, propelled Texas into sole possession of first place in the American League West. "We're just here showing up every day to play and try and get in the playoffs," outfielder Wyatt Langford said. "To be in that position right now is great. But yeah, there are still a lot of games left. We need to keep it that way." While the playoff picture is looking up for Texas, the hopes continue to fade for Toronto (76-79), which has dropped four of its past five. The loss dropped the Blue Jays to three games behind the final wild card in the AL, currently held by the Chicago White Sox, with seven games remaining in the season. Toronto trailed 3-0 after two innings. The Blue Jays didn't get their first baserunner until Vladimir Guerrero Jr. walked in the fourth inning, and didn't get their first hit until the sixth. But pitching struggles in the bottom of the sixth allowed the Rangers to tack on three more runs. "It feels like the last couple games you're down early, and it makes it a little bit tougher to come back," manager John Schneider said. "You're looking for a big swing, a three-run homer or a base hit to score a couple to get back into it. I think falling behind early makes it a little bit tougher." Spencer Miles (6-2, 2.65) will get the start in what is expected to be a bullpen game for Toronto on Sunday. It'll be the second career appearance against Texas for the 26-year-old righty, who gave up just one hit in 2 2/3 innings of a relief appearance in a no-decision versus the Rangers on June 26. --Field Level Media

item.title: Irán advierte de una nueva escalada de Estados Unidos y sus aliados
item.description: Irán advirtió el domingo contra cualquier nuevo ataque de gran envergadura de Estados Unidos y sus aliados, y dijo que disponía de información según la cual se estaba preparando una acción de este tipo, lo que aumentó la inquietud en una región ya sacudida por los ataques con drones y misiles contra Arabia Saudita .
item.dc:creator: Jana Choukeir
item.content:encoded: Irán advirtió el domingo contra cualquier nuevo ataque de gran envergadura de Estados Unidos y sus aliados, y dijo que disponía de información según la cual se estaba preparando una acción de este tipo, lo que aumentó la inquietud en una región ya sacudida por los ataques con drones y misiles contra Arabia Saudita . El mando central militar de Irán dijo en medios de comunicación estatales que cualquier nuevo ataque desencadenaría una represalia sostenida contra las bases y los intereses estadounidenses, y que los aliados regionales de Washington serían considerados partes en el conflicto. No dio más detalles sobre la información de la que, dijo, disponía acerca de un inminente ataque estadounidense. El Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos emitió el sábado una alerta de seguridad en la que indicaba que existía la posibilidad de una escalada imprevista en Oriente Medio y que los estadounidenses debían redoblar la vigilancia y estar atentos a posibles cancelaciones de vuelos y cierres del espacio aéreo. A punto de cumplirse siete meses de la guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irán, ninguna de las partes parece dispuesta a hacer concesiones importantes para poner fin a los combates y, con los mercados energéticos mundiales ya al límite, el conflicto sigue extendiéndose en la región. El sábado, los hutíes de Yemen, respaldados por Irán, dijeron haber llevado a cabo ataques en la capital saudita, Riad, y contra una importante instalación petrolera en el puerto de Yanbu, en el mar Rojo. Arabia Saudita no hizo comentarios sobre el incidente ni sobre las afirmaciones de los hutíes. La alerta del Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos mencionaba las hostilidades de los hutíes contra Arabia Saudita, incluidos los aeropuertos civiles. La reciente escalada de los hutíes ha obligado a Riad a enfrentarse a un doloroso dilema: continuar con los ataques aéreos contra el grupo para impedir que se apodere de más territorio yemení o dar un paso atrás con la esperanza de evitar ataques con drones contra infraestructuras críticas. Los avances de los hutíes a lo largo de la costa significan que las fuerzas del grupo se sitúan ahora en el estrecho de Mandeb, lo que les facilita el control del tráfico marítimo entre el mar Rojo y Asia y les permite bloquear esta vía navegable crucial. Dado que Irán ya ha bloqueado la mayor parte del tráfico marítimo en el estrecho de Ormuz, las exportaciones energéticas del golfo Pérsico, rico en petróleo, están ahora casi totalmente aisladas de los mercados mundiales, lo que aumenta la presión sobre los precios mundiales del petróleo. Por su parte, el bloqueo estadounidense de los puertos iraníes impide a Irán vender su propio petróleo, lo que contribuye a los graves problemas de la economía de la República Islámica. Irán reiteró el domingo que no reabriría el estrecho de Ormuz hasta que se cumplan los términos de un acuerdo de junio, tal y como los interpretaba. El presidente del Parlamento iraní, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, dijo que Irán tendría que seguir luchando, además de negociando, para hacer retroceder a sus enemigos y consolidar cualquier avance logrado mediante la diplomacia.

item.title: Ronald Acuna Jr., Braves bid to clinch NL East in finale vs. Astros
item.description: Atlanta Braves right fielder Ronald Acuna Jr. rode a torrid 20-game stretch into the middle contest Saturday of an interleague series against the Houston Astros, and he continued his stellar play.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Atlanta Braves right fielder Ronald Acuna Jr. rode a torrid 20-game stretch into the middle contest Saturday of an interleague series against the Houston Astros, and he continued his stellar play. Acuna finished 2-for-3 with two walks and a seventh-inning grand slam that sent the Braves toward a 6-3 victory. Atlanta (91-64) has a magic number of one to clinch the National League East title for the seventh time in nine seasons heading into Sunday's series finale in Houston. Acuna was batting .363 with six homers and 16 RBIs over the previous 20 games, a stretch that started after he sat and watched the finale of a three-game series against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Aug. 27. Since then, he has more closely resembled the two-way threat who terrorized the NL before two separate season-ending knee injuries altered his stardom. "And it's understandable, right?" Braves manager Walt Weiss said of Acuna methodically rounding into his superstar form. "When you have both knees reconstructed, it takes time to, not only physically, but mentally have the confidence in really letting it fly. "I think we're seeing that now with Ronald again." Left-hander Martin Perez (9-9, 3.07 ERA) will start the series finale for the Braves. Perez earned his first win in six starts -- and the 100th victory of his career -- in the Braves' 6-3 triumph over the Chicago Cubs on Tuesday, allowing three runs (two earned) on five hits and four walks with two strikeouts over six innings. Perez was 0-3 with a 3.55 ERA in the five starts between wins, and he is 10-8 with a 3.72 ERA in 22 career appearances (21 starts) against the Astros. Right-hander Hunter Brown (6-3, 3.43 ERA) is scheduled to start for the Astros (77-78) as they attempt to avert a three-game series sweep on Sunday. Houston trails the Texas Rangers by one game atop the American League West and is two games behind the Chicago White Sox in the race for the AL's final wild-card spot. Brown matched his season high with 10 strikeouts against the Kansas City Royals on Tuesday, allowing one run on two hits and three walks over five innings in a 4-2 win. He is 3-0 with a 2.86 ERA over his last five starts. Brown is 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA across three career starts against the Braves. He recorded a 6-2 win over them on Sept. 13, 2025, allowing two runs on four hits and one walk with two strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings. Left-hander Steven Okert, Houston's second-most consistent reliever behind closer Josh Hader, has spent the last two weeks on the injured list with a hamstring strain. His absence continues to be felt, as the Astros have struggled with high-leverage situations. Right-hander reliever AJ Blubaugh allowed three runs on two hits and one walk while recording just one out in the seventh inning on Saturday. In seven appearances since Okert went on the IL, Blubaugh has surrendered nine runs on nine hits and five walks over six innings. Right-hander reliever Bryan Abreu allowed a walk-off home run to the Rays' Junior Caminero on Sept. 11 and surrendered the grand slam to Acuna that flipped the game on Saturday. Previously reliable relievers Blubaugh and Abreu -- in tandem with Okert -- have labored lately. "Those are our guys, and I trust them," Astros manager Joe Espada said. "And I'm going to continue to give them the ball." --Field Level Media

item.title: Iran warns against new escalation by US and allies
item.description: Iran said it had information such a move was being prepared, adding to the anxiety in a region already on edge after drone and missile strikes on Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Jana Choukeir
item.content:encoded: Iran warned on Sunday against any big new attack by the United States and its allies, saying it had information such a move was being prepared, adding to the anxiety in a region already on edge after drone and missile strikes [USN:L1N45B003 TEXT:"on Saudi Arabia"]. Iran's military central command said on state media that any new attack would trigger sustained retaliation against US bases and interests, and that Washington's regional allies would be considered parties to the conflict. It did not elaborate on the information it said it had about a coming US attack. The US State Department issued a security alert on Saturday saying there was potential for unforeseen escalation in the Middle East and Americans should exercise more vigilance and be aware of possible flight cancellations and airspace closures. Nearly seven months into the US-Iran war , neither side has looked ready to make major concessions needed to end the fighting and with global energy markets already stretched, the conflict continues to spill over into other crises around the region. On Saturday Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis, who made major advances along Yemen's Red Sea coast after the country's civil war reignited this month, said they had carried out strikes in the Saudi capital Riyadh and on a major oil facility in the kingdom's Red Sea port of Yanbu. Reuters video showed a massive plume of black smoke billowing from the area of Riyadh's main international airport after booms were heard in the Saudi capital overnight. Saudi Arabia did not comment on the incident or the Houthi claims, though a Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had foiled other attacks on the kingdom. The US State Department alert cited Houthi hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports. Recent escalation by the Houthis has forced Riyadh into a painful dilemma: continue airstrikes on the group to stop it seizing more Yemeni territory or step back in the hopes of averting drone strikes on critical infrastructure. STRIKES ON SAUDI ARABIA The Houthi gains along the coast mean the group's forces now sit on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, giving them easier control over shipping travelling between the Red Sea and Asia and the ability to blockade the crucial waterway. With Iran already having blockaded most shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, the oil-rich Gulf's energy exports are now almost entirely cut off from global markets, adding to pressure on global oil prices. A US blockade of Iranian ports is meanwhile stopping Iran from selling its own oil, contributing to [USN:L1N44W081 TEXT:"major problems"] in the Islamic Republic's economy. With the war inflicting painful damage on all sides, however, there is little sign of a return to the interim ceasefire agreement that was struck in June but that [USN:L6N43F0R2 TEXT:"fell apart"] in July amid disputes over its terms. Iran reiterated on Sunday that it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the terms of that June agreement, as it interpreted them, were met. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said Iran would have to keep on fighting as well as negotiating, to push back its enemies and to consolidate any gains with diplomacy.

item.title: Un Israélien et un Palestinien abattus en Cisjordanie occupée
item.description: Un Israélien a été abattu dimanche en Cisjordanie occupée par un tireur palestinien présumé, a rapporté la police, tandis que des soldats israéliens ont tué un automobiliste palestinien qui, selon l'armée, tentait de les renverser.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Un Israélien a été abattu dimanche en Cisjordanie occupée par un tireur palestinien présumé, a rapporté la police, tandis que des soldats israéliens ont tué un automobiliste palestinien qui, selon l'armée, tentait de les renverser. Selon l'armée et la police israéliennes, le tireur a ouvert le feu depuis son véhicule sur des Israéliens rassemblés à proximité de la colonie de Neve Tzuf, près de Ramallah. Un homme grièvement blessé par balle a été déclaré mort à l'hôpital, a déclaré la police. Le tireur a été localisé quelques heures plus tard dans un hôpital de Ramallah et arrêté, a-t-elle ajouté. Peu après la fusillade, l'armée a annoncé avoir "éliminé" un automobiliste palestinien qui avait tenté de lancer sa voiture sur des soldats près de la colonie de Ganim, plus au nord en Cisjordanie. Aucun soldat n'a été blessé, a-t-elle ajouté.

item.title: El hermano de Diana compara trato que medios dan a Enrique y Meghan con el que sufrió la princesa
item.description: El trato que los medios de comunicación han dispensado al príncipe Enrique y a su esposa Meghan es comparable al que sufrió su madre, Diana, dijo el hermano de la difunta princesa en una entrevista publicada el domingo, en la que advirtió de que era necesario aprender de aquella época.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El trato que los medios de comunicación han dispensado al príncipe Enrique y a su esposa Meghan es comparable al que sufrió su madre, Diana, dijo el hermano de la difunta princesa en una entrevista publicada el domingo, en la que advirtió de que era necesario aprender de aquella época. Diana falleció a los 36 años en un accidente de tráfico en París en 1997, mientras unos fotógrafos la perseguían en moto, lo que desencadenó una oleada de dolor y un debate sobre si los medios de comunicación tenían alguna responsabilidad en su muerte. "Si te fijas en una noticia de un tabloide sobre Diana o sobre la pareja que mencionabas, Enrique y Meghan, ya sabes, pueden ser realmente, realmente desagradables", dijo a la BBC el hermano de Diana, el conde Charles Spencer. "Y creo que la gente debería aprender del ejemplo de Diana". "No estoy aquí para hablar en nombre de Enrique y Meghan, pero para cualquiera que esté siendo destrozado de esta manera a diario, debe de ser una influencia cancerosa en su vida", dijo. Enrique, el hijo menor de Diana, y Meghan, mencionaron el impacto de lo que ellos denominaban "medios tóxicos" tenía en sus vidas antes de renunciar a sus obligaciones reales y mudarse a Estados Unidos en 2020. También demandaron a gran parte de la prensa sensacionalista británica —con diversos grados de éxito— antes de regresar a Gran Bretaña en agosto. Spencer ha acaparado los titulares de todo el mundo durante la última semana después de que su libro, «Swan Song: Diana, My Sister», se publicara por entregas en el Daily Mail, en el que acusaba a su exmarido, el ahora rey Carlos, de mostrarse «eufórico» en las horas posteriores a su muerte. El palacio respondió afirmando que el rey «es consciente de que el dolor de la pérdida de un hermano puede nublar la razón, afectar al juicio y sesgar los recuerdos de formas que los demás no perciben, incluso muchos años después de dicha pérdida». La publicación del libro y el regreso de Harry y Meghan a Gran Bretaña suponen otro reto para el rey, que sigue sometiéndose a tratamiento contra el cáncer. La familia de Diana acusó a la familia real de mostrar una falta de apoyo o de atención hacia la difunta princesa antes de su muerte, una acusación que repitió Harry, quien actualmente se encuentra en gran medida distanciado del resto de la familia real.

item.title: Resurgent Acosta beats Martin for maiden MotoGP win in Austria
item.description: Pedro Acosta claimed the first MotoGP victory of his career in the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday, bouncing back from his sprint-race crash to beat world championship leader Jorge Martin at KTM's home Red Bull Ring circuit.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pedro Acosta claimed the first MotoGP victory of his career in the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday, bouncing back from his [USN:L1N45B02X TEXT:"sprint-race"] crash to beat world championship leader Jorge Martin at KTM's home Red Bull Ring circuit. The 22-year-old Spaniard, who qualified third before crashing out while leading Saturday's sprint, seized the lead from [USN:L4N45B027 TEXT:"polesitter Martin"] on lap nine of the 28-lap race and never looked back. Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi completed the podium, while Trackhouse rider Ai Ogura finished fourth. It was an emotional moment for Acosta, nicknamed 'The Shark', who arrived in MotoGP with huge expectations after winning the Moto3 world title in 2021 and the Moto2 crown in 2023. "The first one is always special," Acosta said. "Nice way to close a season like this with KTM in front of all Austrian fans. Super happy for them because they deserve it even more than me." Acosta is set to leave KTM at the end of 2026 to join the factory Ducati team. Martin, the 2024 MotoGP champion, got off to a brilliant start but was overtaken by teammate Bezzecchi for the lead at Turn One on lap two. The 28-year-old responded immediately, reclaiming top spot at Turn Three on the same lap. However, Acosta's pace proved decisive and he passed Martin for the lead on lap nine before pulling away. "I want to congratulate Pedro. He fought a lot during the last few years to get this victory. This feeling is amazing for him, so I'm really happy for him," Martin said of his fellow Spaniard. "For myself, I think I did a great race. I was trying to manage the fuel. Then Pedro took me but I thought everything was under control. But step by step, he was stepping away. I tried to push a bit more but my rear tyre was completely destroyed. I did my best. "This is what we have to do every weekend for the rest of the season, and the fight is on. So I am really looking forward to continuing like this." Martin now has 306 points in the standings, a 12-point lead over compatriot and reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez ahead of next month's Japanese Grand Prix. Italian Bezzecchi is third with 264 points. Marquez endured a frustrating weekend as Ducati lacked the outright pace of the Aprilias. The seven-time MotoGP champion qualified second but slipped back on the opening lap and eventually finished fifth.

item.title: Cubs eye potential playoff berth in finale vs. Reds
item.description: The Chicago Cubs could not ask for a better gift than a healthy Dansby Swanson for the playoffs.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago Cubs could not ask for a better gift than a healthy Dansby Swanson for the playoffs. Swanson came off the injured list on Friday after being sidelined for a month with a left oblique strain. On Saturday, he hit his 19th home run of the season to help the visiting Cubs record a 5-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds. Chicago (86-69) can clinch a playoff spot with a win on Sunday afternoon against the Reds and a loss by the Arizona Diamondbacks to the New York Yankees. The Cubs are tied with the San Diego Padres (86-69) in the race for the top wild-card spot in the National League, one game ahead of the Philadelphia Phillies (85-70) and five games ahead of Arizona (81-74). "This is like uncharted territory for me," Swanson said. "I'm just grateful for all the support from the team. Today was just a complete effort from everyone. I love when (reliever Daniel) Palencia is out there and believes no one can hit him. That is when he is best." Palencia retired all six batters he faced in two innings on Saturday, striking out three. "His two innings were his best outing of the year," Cubs manager Craig Counsell said of Palencia. "Through this last week, we have to find out about our bullpen, and this was a good step in that direction." The bullpen took over for Matthew Boyd, who allowed two runs on two hits in five innings to pick up his first win since Aug. 9. Four relievers allowed only two hits the rest of the way. "If we want to be a team that plays for a long time, we need to get outs from the bullpen," Counsell said. "We have to figure out who is going to get it done." The Cubs are expected to send left-hander David Peterson (8-8, 5.11 ERA) to the mound on Sunday. He is coming off a solid start in which he allowed one earned run on three hits in six innings of a 7-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves on Monday. The 31-year-old is 1-2 with a 5.84 ERA in eight career appearances (seven starts) vs. Cincinnati (72-83), which has been eliminated from playoff contention and will counter with right-hander Rhett Lowder (6-11, 5.79 ERA) on Sunday. Lowder's last win came on Aug. 28, a 10-8 decision over the Cubs. He yielded three runs on six hits in five innings to improve to 1-1 with a 3.60 ERA in four career meetings (three starts) vs. Chicago. The 24-year-old is coming off a 4-0 loss to the Dodgers on Tuesday in a game in which he gave up three runs and five hits in five innings. The Reds rallied to forge a 2-2 tie on Saturday with two runs in the fifth inning before the game slipped away. "The only thing I would say is I'm jealous," Cincinnati manager Terry Francona said. "Me and Nap (bench coach Mike Napoli) were talking (Friday) night. We were looking at the scoreboard, like, man, that feeling of anxiety. I kind of miss that." --Field Level Media

item.title: USA Trump transforme son projet d'arc de triomphe en "complexe militaire"
item.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré dimanche avoir accepté, à la demande de l'armée, de convertir son projet d'arc de triomphe à Washington en complexe militaire chargé d'abriter et déployer drones et munitions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré dimanche avoir accepté, à la demande de l'armée, de convertir son projet d'arc de triomphe à Washington en complexe militaire chargé d'abriter et déployer drones et munitions. Le président américain a mentionné des préoccupations de sécurité nationale à l'appui de cette décision, sans mentionner de menaces spécifiques. Donald Trump a déjà modifié son projet de salle de bal à la Maison blanche, contesté devant la justice, et le présente désormais comme un complexe militaire intégré nécessaire à la sécurité nationale. L'autorité américaine de l'aviation civile a estimé vendredi que le projet d'un arc de triomphe d'une hauteur de 76 mètres près du cimetière national d'Arlington ne présentait pas de risque pour l'aviation civile à condition qu'il soit surmonté en permanence de spots éclairants. Des experts en aéronautique avaient émis des inquiétudes quant au choix du site, non loin de l'aéroport Ronald-Reagan. Des anciens combattants ont également déposé un recours contre le projet en estimant qu'il abîmerait la perspective entre le Lincoln Memorial et le cimetière d'Arlington. Depuis le début de son second mandat en janvier 2025, Donald Trump a entrepris de remodeler en profondeur la capitale fédérale avec la volonté d'y laisser son empreinte. Outre la destruction de l'aile Est de la Maison blanche pour y construire sa salle de bal, le président américain a fait rénover le bassin réfléchissant du Lincoln Memorial, désormais recouvert d'algues, et menace de démolir le Kennedy Center, haut lieu culturel de la ville, depuis que la justice lui a refusé d'y accoler son nom.

item.title: Macron y Carney se reunirán en un archipiélago francés del Atlántico, en un gesto dirigido a Trump
item.description: El presidente Emmanuel Macron llegó el domingo al territorio francés de San Pedro y Miquelón para mantener conversaciones con el primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, semanas después de que el presidente Donald Trump publicó una imagen en la que se veía a las islas cubiertas por la bandera estadounidense.
item.dc:creator: John Irish
item.content:encoded: El presidente Emmanuel Macron llegó el domingo al territorio francés de San Pedro y Miquelón para mantener conversaciones con el primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, semanas después de que el presidente Donald Trump publicó una imagen en la que se veía a las islas cubiertas por la bandera estadounidense. La visita de Macron al archipiélago situado frente a la costa atlántica de Canadá es la primera que realiza un presidente francés desde 2014 y coincide con un acercamiento de Canadá a la Unión Europea en un contexto de una guerra comercial cada vez más encarnizada con Estados Unidos. San Pedro y Miquelón es el único territorio que le queda a Francia en Norteamérica, y las autoridades francesas dijeron que el viaje de Macron subrayaría la soberanía francesa y pondría de relieve los estrechos vínculos con Canadá. "No hay duda (de que es francés)", dijo Macron tras aterrizar el sábado por la noche en este territorio de 5.800 habitantes. "No vamos a afirmarlo todos los días porque la gente tenga ideas extrañas o diga cosas raras", dijo a periodistas en respuesta a una pregunta sobre el mapa de Trump. LA VISITA TIENE UN PESO SIMBÓLICO Los diplomáticos señalaron que la visita de Macron, que se dirigía a la Asamblea General anual de las Naciones Unidas en la que se reúnen los líderes mundiales, tenía un peso simbólico tras la publicación de Trump en las redes sociales. La imagen que compartió Trump mostraba la bandera de Estados Unidos extendida sobre Estados Unidos, Canadá, Groenlandia, Islandia, México, Centroamérica y el Caribe, y llevaba la leyenda "Estados Unidos de América". Incluía San Pedro y Miquelón y los territorios franceses del Caribe. Francia no respondió públicamente a la publicación en ese momento. Para Francia, San Pedro y Miquelón reviste una importancia estratégica debido a su ubicación a las puertas de Estados Unidos y del Ártico, explicó un responsable de la Presidencia francesa a los periodistas en una rueda de prensa previa a la visita. El territorio también ocupa un lugar clave en la cooperación de Francia con Canadá, entre otros ámbitos, en materia de energía, uno de los temas centrales de la reunión del domingo entre Macron y Carney.

item.title: White Sox continue push toward playoffs in finale against Tigers
item.description: Heading into the finale of a four-game set against the Detroit Tigers on Sunday afternoon, the host Chicago White Sox are desperate for a hero.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Heading into the finale of a four-game set against the Detroit Tigers on Sunday afternoon, the host Chicago White Sox are desperate for a hero. Miguel Vargas wants to fill that spot. The All-Star slugged his 33rd home run of the season on Saturday to help Chicago (79-76) beat Detroit 3-1 and stay a game behind the Cleveland Guardians atop the American League Central. The White Sox hold a two-game lead over the Houston Astros in the race for the third and final AL wild-card berth. "That's what I work for. That's why I wake up every day and work so hard for these types of moments," Vargas said. "And for me, this group has been pushing me every single day. I've never been thinking about my individual stats. I just want to go out there and do the best for my team and have some fun and always try hard." Davis Martin (9-7, 3.96 ERA) will make his fourth appearance since being activated from the 15-day injured list (finger blister). The right-hander has a 1.13 ERA in three outings since his return, giving up just three runs (two earned), but he has only an 0-1 record to show for it. Martin threw 5 1/3 innings of one-run, two-hit ball against Cleveland on Tuesday in a no-decision. He entered after Chris Murphy gave up three runs in two-thirds of an inning as the opener in Chicago's 7-6 loss. Martin is 1-2 with a 3.49 ERA in seven career games (six starts) against the Tigers. The 29-year-old surrendered just one run on five hits across six innings in Detroit on June 21, striking out four and walking three in a no-decision. Chicago lost 5-4 in 10 innings. On June 10, Martin had a 9-2 record and a 2.41 ERA after a 2-1 win over the Atlanta Braves. He has not won since, piling up five losses and nine no-decisions. Meanwhile, Detroit (73-82) is nearing the mathematical end to a disappointing season. After consecutive playoff appearances, the Tigers will be eliminated from postseason contention with their next loss. Detroit left 11 runners on base in the club's third loss in four games on Saturday. "It feels good to have opportunities. It doesn't feel good when you miss out on them," Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said. "It's tough when you leave that many on, but you don't want to not have them on there and not have the chance." As he makes his 20th start of the season for Detroit on Sunday, right-hander Troy Melton (8-4, 2.52 ERA) is looking to improve on what has been a forgettable September. After posting a 2.10 ERA in August, the 25-year-old has allowed 11 earned runs in 13 2/3 innings across his past three starts. On Monday, Melton lasted just 2 2/3 innings against the Toronto Blue Jays. He gave up two runs on five hits while walking four and striking out three in a no-decision. He needed 76 pitches to record eight outs in a game the Tigers won 6-5. In five career appearances (four starts) against the White Sox, Melton is 2-0 with a 1.48 ERA. He has faced them three times this year, going 1-0 with a 1.56 ERA, allowing three earned runs in 17 1/3 innings. The Tigers are 1-2 in his starts against the White Sox. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ucrania lanza el mayor ataque con drones contra Moscú, durante las elecciones en Rusia
item.description: Ucrania lanzó el domingo lo que el alcalde de Moscú calificó como el mayor ataque con drones hasta la fecha contra la capital rusa, mientras los rusos votaban en la última jornada de unas elecciones parlamentarias que el presidente Vladimir Putin ha presentado como una prueba del apoyo a la guerra.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Osborn, Vladimir Soldatkin
item.content:encoded: Ucrania lanzó el domingo lo que el alcalde de Moscú calificó como el mayor ataque con drones hasta la fecha contra la capital rusa, mientras los rusos votaban en la última jornada de unas elecciones parlamentarias que el presidente Vladimir Putin ha presentado como una prueba del apoyo a la guerra. Los ataques con drones causaron la muerte de dos personas en la región de Moscú y otras dos en la parte de la región ucraniana de Jersón controlada por Rusia, entre ellas un funcionario electoral, según el alcalde de Moscú, Serguéi Sobianin, y las autoridades electorales. Ademas, resultó dañada una instalación de la refinería de petróleo de Moscú, que ya había sido objeto de bombardeos. "Se ha repelido el mayor ataque de drones enemigos", dijo Sobianin en Telegram. "Este ataque sin precedentes fue claramente planeado con el objetivo de perturbar las elecciones. El enemigo no lo ha conseguido". En las elecciones a la Duma Estatal, las primeras desde que Rusia inició su guerra a gran escala en Ucrania en febrero de 2022, se espera que el partido gobernante, Rusia Unida, conserve fácilmente su dominio en un sistema político que, según los críticos, no tolera la disidencia. Es probable que el Kremlin presente el resultado como prueba del respaldo público a las políticas de Putin y a la guerra, que ya entra en su quinto año sin que haya indicios de que vaya a terminar pronto. Las autoridades electorales han dicho que los tres días de votaciones se han desarrollado sin incidentes, a pesar de los ciberataques. A última hora de la mañana del domingo, la participación superaba el 45% tanto en las elecciones a la Duma como en las regionales, informó la presidenta de la Comisión Electoral Central, Ella Pamfilova. A la mayoría de los candidatos contrarios a la guerra se les ha prohibido presentarse a las elecciones. Los que sí se presentaron, pertenecientes al partido liberal Yabloko, dijeron que temían por su libertad, después de que los tribunales condenaron a largas penas de cárcel a dos figuras destacadas del partido antes de las elecciones por sus comentarios sobre el conflicto. Desacreditar al ejército o difundir lo que las autoridades consideran "noticias falsas" se castiga con largas penas de prisión. En un pequeño acto de rebeldía, el líder de Yabloko, Nikolai Rybakov, anuló de forma ostensible su papeleta, escribiendo el nombre de su partido y el lema "Por la paz". El Kremlin dice que la unidad nacional y cierta censura son necesarias durante lo que denomina su "operación militar especial" en Ucrania, que presenta el conflicto —el más mortífero de Europa desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial— como parte de una lucha existencial contra un Occidente hostil.

item.title: Luxembourg deploys additional detection assets following drone sightings
item.description: Luxembourg's government said on Sunday that additional detection assets have been deployed to strengthen airspace monitoring, after Luxembourg Airport temporarily suspended services late on Friday due to the sighting of drones.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Luxembourg's government said on Sunday that additional detection assets have been deployed to strengthen airspace monitoring, after Luxembourg Airport temporarily suspended services late on Friday due to the sighting of drones. "To strengthen airspace monitoring and analysis capabilities, additional detection assets have been deployed, including resources provided by foreign partners," the government said in a statement. "These supplementary systems have contributed to further consolidating airspace surveillance and contributed to a better assessment of the situation by the competent authorities," it added. The government also said that on Saturday evening police "received several reports concerning the suspected presence of drones within national airspace" but that "following verifications, no situation required an operational intervention by the authorities". Luxembourg's authorities launched an investigation after flight operations had been temporarily suspended on Friday evening following the visual sighting of "unidentified and unauthorized drones". Prime Minister Luc Frieden told reporters on Saturday that his country had been "confronted with something new for Luxembourg, the presence of potentially bigger drones in the Luxembourg airspace". "We have observed this over the past few days, which led to the precautionary measure last night," he said. On Sunday, Luxembourg's government said its drone assessment cell is continuing work with partners to ensure monitoring of the situation.

item.title: Italy to ban veils in schools, limit foreign students per class, Meloni says
item.description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni played up her right-wing credentials at a youth event organized by her party.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy is preparing to ban face coverings in schools and to cap the number of foreign students per class, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said on Sunday as she played up her right-wing credentials at a youth event organised by her party. Italy is among the European countries most exposed to migrant arrivals because of its central Mediterranean location, making migration a hot-button issue and a major challenge for successive governments. The integration of migrants, particularly those from Muslim-majority countries, remains contentious in Italian politics and society. Debates over religious symbols, cultural integration, citizenship rules and immigration policy frequently polarize public opinion. "A measure will soon be presented to a Cabinet meeting to legally establish a maximum number of foreign students per class. It also requires parents of foreign students facing serious difficulties integrating into the school system to learn Italian and bans burqas and niqabs in schools," Meloni told an annual gathering of the youth wing of her Brothers of Italy party. "If there is only one child in a class who doesn't understand Italian, that child will likely be able to learn the language and integrate quickly with the help of classmates and teachers. However, if the number of children who don't understand the language becomes large - or even the majority - that is no longer integration; it is neglect," she added. Meloni did not specify what the maximum number of foreign students per class would be. Students who are not Italian citizens account for 11.6% of those enrolled in Italian schools — nearly 12 in every 100 students — according to Fondazione ISMU, a research institution. "You must go to school with your face uncovered, and in Italy no one, in the name of a real or supposed tradition, can decide that a young woman must hide herself, " Meloni said.

item.title: Iran seals French language centre in Tehran, accuses it of illegal activities
item.description: Iranian authorities have sealed a French language centre affiliated with the French embassy in Tehran following a judicial order, the Tehran prosecutor's office said on Sunday according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iranian authorities have sealed a French language centre affiliated with the French embassy in Tehran following a judicial order, the Tehran prosecutor's office said on Sunday according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. The centre operated for years under the cover of foreign-language teaching despite repeated warnings to obtain a licence, authorities said, accusing it of activities against Iranian culture and national security, including identifying and building networks as well as facilitating the departure of skilled Iranians from the country.

item.title: Palestinian gunman shoots dead Israeli in the West Bank, soldiers kill motorist
item.description: It was not clear whether the incidents on the eve of Yom Kippur were connected.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Violence flared in the occupied West Bank on Sunday when a suspected Palestinian gunman shot dead an Israeli man, police said, and Israeli soldiers killed a Palestinian motorist who the military said was attempting to run them over. The gunman opened fire from his vehicle at Israelis gathered at a spring near the settlement of Neve Tzuf, near Ramallah, according to the Israeli military and police. Medics who arrived at the scene of the shooting said they found a man in a car suffering from critical gunshot wounds. He was pronounced dead at hospital, police said. The gunman was located a few hours later at a hospital in Ramallah and arrested, police said. Shortly after the shooting, the military said that its forces "eliminated" a Palestinian driver who had attempted a ramming attack on soldiers near the settlement of Ganim, further north in the West Bank. No soldiers were hurt, it said. Reuters was not able to immediately verify the soldiers' account. It was not clear whether the fatal incidents, on the eve of the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur, were connected. Following the incidents, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had instructed security agencies to beef up their forces and carry out arrests and offensive activities in the area. Palestinian militant group Hamas praised the shooting attack but did not claim responsibility for it. Violence has escalated in the West Bank since Hamas' October 7, 2023, attack on Israel and the ensuing Israeli military offensive in Gaza . The West Bank violence has included a sharp rise in attacks by [USN:L6N44Y077 TEXT:"militant settlers"] on Palestinians, as well as sweeping Israeli military raids and Palestinian attacks on Israelis.

item.title: Trump to use Washington triumphal arch as military complex
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday the triumphal arch he plans to build near Arlington National Cemetery in Washington would double as a "military complex" housing drones and snipers, as well as storing large quantities of ammunition.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday the triumphal arch he plans to build near Arlington National Cemetery in Washington would double as a "military complex" housing drones and snipers, as well as storing large quantities of ammunition. The president cited national security concerns for the move, echoing the rationale offered for the roughly $400 million ballroom complex being built on the site of the White House's former East Wing, which was demolished to make way for the project. He did not identify any specific threats. The projects are part of Trump's ambitious effort to [USN:L6N41H110 TEXT:"reshape Washington"], including a push to add his name to the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. The plans have drawn criticism from preservationists and others who argue they could alter or diminish historic landmarks. In a social media post, Trump said that at the "strong request" of the military he had agreed to turn the 250-foot (76-meter) arch "into a top grade Military Complex/Triumphal Arch, to house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas, and additionally have and hold large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage." The White House and the Department of Defense did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Federal Aviation Administration said last week that the arch would [USN:L1N45A0PQ TEXT:"not pose a hazard"] to aircraft but would be required to have an "eternal flame" on top, clearing an aviation hurdle for the arch, which Trump proposed to mark the nation's 250th anniversary. Aviation experts have raised safety concerns given its proximity to Reagan Washington National Airport while veterans have sued to block the arch, arguing it would destroy the historic sightline between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

item.title: Pirates' Brandon Lowe takes HR barrage into finale vs. Royals
item.description: The Pittsburgh Pirates will look to complete a three-game sweep of the visiting Kansas City Royals on Sunday afternoon behind Brandon Lowe, who has homered in four of his last five games.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Pittsburgh Pirates will look to complete a three-game sweep of the visiting Kansas City Royals on Sunday afternoon behind Brandon Lowe, who has homered in four of his last five games. Lowe's two-run homer in the eighth inning on Saturday lifted Pittsburgh (78-77) to a 6-5 victory over Kansas City (67-88). The win was the Pirates' 13th in their last 19 games. Lowe's 33rd homer was the 96th hit by the club at home this season, breaking a franchise mark established in 1947. It also was Lowe's 19th homer at home, eclipsing Brian Giles' club mark, set in 2001. "The best part of it is coming out with a win," Lowe said. "Records are cool, but a win is a whole lot better." Even though the Pirates were eliminated from playoff contention on Friday, Lowe said the team has plenty of reasons to compete. "It's never too late to get hot," he said. "It's a good time to get rolling and keep playing some good baseball ... The postseason thing won't happen, and that stinks. But we are still playing meaningful baseball when it comes to what the future of this organization can do. Winning is a whole lot better than losing." Right-hander Lake Bachar (1-4, 3.50 ERA) will start for the Pirates on Sunday despite pitching one scoreless inning of relief on Saturday. Bachar is 1-0 with a 4.50 ERA in two relief appearances vs. the Royals. Kansas City will counter with right-hander Michael Wacha (9-9, 3.34 ERA), who will look to add to his career-high innings total. Wacha, a 14-year veteran, set a career high for innings pitched on Sept. 8. He surpassed his previous mark of 181 1/3 innings, set in 2015 with the St. Louis Cardinals. Royals manager Matt Quatraro praised Wacha -- who has 20 quality starts this season -- for his consistency. "You can pencil him in for six (innings) every time out, if not more," Quatraro said. "... He has got really good stuff, he pitches down with the sinker, up with the four-seamer." In his last start, Wacha took the loss, surrendering four runs on four hits with a walk and two strikeouts in a 4-2 road setback against the Houston Astros on Tuesday. Wacha is 8-3 with a 3.59 ERA in 19 career appearances (17 starts) against the Pirates. Carter Jensen launched his 25th home run of the season on Saturday, a solo shot in the third inning that established a rookie home run standard for the Royals. Bob Hamelin had held the record since 1994. "He's a good player; I'm happy for him and his family," Quatraro said of Jensen. "That's an accomplishment that is going to be there for a long time, I imagine. The future is extremely bright for him." --Field Level Media

item.title: European Commissioner discussed EU-Israel relationship, Gaza with Israeli minister
item.description: The European Commissioner for the Mediterranean said on Sunday that she discussed the European Union's relationship with Israel, regional stability and Gaza recovery efforts with Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The European Commissioner for the Mediterranean said on Sunday that she discussed the European Union's relationship with Israel, regional stability and Gaza recovery efforts with Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar. Dubravka Suica said in a post on X after the call that they discussed EU-Israel "relations and our shared interest in security and stability across the Middle East. This includes a reformed and functioning Palestinian Authority". When it comes to Gaza, "I focused on the urgent need to advance early recovery," she said, adding that "our continued cooperation is key to delivering early recovery projects on the ground". The commissioner announced in July that the EU and like-minded partners launched an initiative to help fund Gaza's early recovery focused on restoring essential social and economic services, rehabilitating critical infrastructure and strengthening governance. The EU has criticised Israel's conduct in the war in Gaza while reaffirming Israel's right to defend itself. It has also criticised Israel's [USN:L8N42P0ZR TEXT:"expansion of Jewish settlements"] in the West Bank, widely viewed as illegal under international law and as an obstacle to Israeli-Palestinian peace and the establishment of a Palestinian state. But the EU's 27 member states are divided, with some highly critical of Israel and others maintaining close ties. Saar said in June that he was severing "all contact" with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas over what he said were remarks attributed to her comparing Israel to apartheid-era South Africa.

item.title: Mets' Carson Benge eager to continue hit parade in matchup vs. Phillies
item.description: The New York Mets spent the first half of their final homestand being reminded of what they were missing without Pete Alonso.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The New York Mets spent the first half of their final homestand being reminded of what they were missing without Pete Alonso. Carson Benge is closing the home schedule by providing the Mets a hint of what they'll have for the foreseeable future. Benge and the Mets will look to end their home slate on a winning note on Sunday afternoon when they face the Philadelphia Phillies in the finale of a four-game series. Mets right-hander Jonah Tong (2-1, 3.43 ERA) will oppose Phillies left-hander Cristopher Sanchez (17-6, 2.93). Benge helped the Mets hurt the Phillies' chances of being in the top wild-card spot in the National League on Saturday, when the rookie outfielder homered among his three hits in a 10-3 victory. The win was the second straight for the Mets (71-84) following a five-game losing streak that included a three-game sweep by Alonso and the Baltimore Orioles. Alonso set the Mets' all-time record with 264 homers before signing with the Orioles as a free agent in December. He received standing ovations before every at-bat in Monday's 2-1 Baltimore win before he hit his 300th career homer in the ninth inning of Tuesday's 7-5 victory in 11 innings. The slugger went deep again in Wednesday's 7-1 rout. But Benge nudged ahead of Alonso in one category in the Mets' record book Saturday, when his three hits gave him 156 this season, breaking the rookie high of 155 set by Alonso in 2019. Benge's record-breaking performance is doubly impressive considering he opened the season with just 17 hits in his first 90 at-bats through April 30. He is batting .292 since May 1. "I came in knowing I belonged," Benge said. "It was kind of rough there in the beginning, but (he was) sticking to my path and grinding out every day and now finally showing others that I finally belong here, too." Benge's big day may have made the playoff path more difficult for the Phillies (85-70), who have lost 10 of their last 16 games to fall into the NL's third wild-card spot. The Phillies are one game behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres, who earned wins later Saturday over the Cincinnati Reds and Miami Marlins, respectively. The final wild card will open the playoffs at the No. 3 seed, likely the NL East-leading Atlanta Braves, who are four games behind the Los Angeles Dodgers in the race for the second seed and final bye in the first round. The Phillies have a four-game wild-card edge over the Arizona Diamondbacks, who beat the New York Yankees on Saturday night. "I just don't think these guys are going to sit back and panic," Philadelphia interim manager Don Mattingly said. "We're in a better spot than a lot of teams, so I think we're positive on it. Honestly, we know what we're capable of." Tong didn't factor into the decision in his most recent start last Monday, when he allowed an unearned run over six innings in the Mets' 2-1 loss to the Orioles. He has yet to face the Phillies in his career. Sanchez took the defeat Tuesday after giving up five runs over 6 1/3 innings in Philadelphia's 6-3 loss to the Washington Nationals. He is 4-4 with a 3.97 ERA in 13 career games (10 starts) against the Mets. --Field Level Media

item.title: Chile's Bachelet withdraws from race to lead UN
item.description: Former Chilean president Michelle Bachelet announced on Saturday that she is withdrawing her candidacy to become the next secretary-general of the United Nations, ending a bid that had struggled to gain traction among Security Council members.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former Chilean president Michelle Bachelet announced on Saturday that she is withdrawing her candidacy to become the next secretary-general of the United Nations, ending a bid that had struggled to gain traction among Security Council members. Bachelet, 74, announced her decision in a video posted on Instagram, saying, "I will now continue, with the same determination as always, my international work." The two-time Chilean president and former UN human rights chief had positioned her campaign around defending multilateralism and international law at a time she said both were under sustained pressure. Bachelet's exit leaves seven candidates in the race to succeed Secretary-General António Guterres, who will conclude his second five-year term on December 31, 2026. It is still possible for more candidates to enter the contest. Her withdrawal comes just a day after a third informal [USN:L6N45A0Z7 TEXT:"straw poll"], held Friday, showed her support had all but collapsed. The same poll put Costa Rica's [USN:L1N44I0L2 TEXT:"Rebeca Grynspan"] in the lead. The UN Security Council will eventually formally recommend a single candidate to the 193-member General Assembly for election. The Assembly's approval has long been seen as a formality once the Council reaches consensus.

item.title: Volvo Cars appoints Klaus Zellmer to succeed Samuelsson as CEO
item.description: Volvo Cars said on Sunday that Klaus Zellmer would become its president and chief executive officer within a year, succeeding Hakan Samuelsson who was reappointed in 2025 with the aim of reviving the Swedish automaker's fortunes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Volvo Cars (VOLCARb.ST) said on Sunday that Klaus Zellmer would become its president and chief executive officer within a year, succeeding Hakan Samuelsson who was reappointed in 2025 with the aim of reviving the Swedish automaker's fortunes. Zellmer will start in his role no later than October 1, 2027, the company said. Samuelsson said last week he had[USN:S8N42K02H TEXT:" no plans to work full time"] after his contract runs out in April. Volvo Cars held a strategy day on Thursday where Samuelsson [USN:L6N45909J TEXT:"laid out an ambitious strategy"] to launch 13 new models between now and 2030 to double the company's market share as the automaker grapples with the fallout of U.S. tariffs and slumping sales in China. The Sweden-based automaker, which is majority-owned by China's Geely Holding [RIC:RIC:GEELY.UL], has struggled to meet previous profitability targets due to tariffs , weaker EV demand and high development costs. It faces an increasingly delicate balancing act separating its Western and Chinese technologies in order to continue selling in the United States, where its sister brand Polestar faces a sales ban. Its shares, which Samuelsson was tasked with reviving when he [USN:L2N3QD031 TEXT:"returned"] for his second stint as CEO, having previously led the company from 2012 to 2022, have continued to trade near record lows and are down more than 45% so far this year.

item.title: Iraqi court opens trial of six French Islamic State suspects
item.description: An Iraqi court on Sunday opened the trial of six French nationals accused of belonging to Islamic State, with a member of the Supreme Judicial Council telling the court that the suspects could face the death penalty if convicted of crimes committed against Iraq and the Iraqi people.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An Iraqi court on Sunday opened the trial of six French nationals accused of belonging to Islamic State, with a member of the Supreme Judicial Council telling the court that the suspects could face the death penalty if convicted of crimes committed against Iraq and the Iraqi people. Two court legal sources said the defendants were among 47 French Islamic State detainees transferred from prisons in northeast Syria last year as part of a broader relocation process overseen by US forces and Iraqi authorities. The French embassy in Baghdad did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Officials from the embassy were present at the Baghdad criminal court, according to a Reuters witness inside the court. The six men, who are being tried under Iraq's counter-terrorism law, arrived at the court in a prison van escorted by a convoy of Humvees carrying Iraqi special forces personnel. The men were dressed in yellow prison jumpsuits. The presiding judge adjourned the hearing until October 5 to allow defence lawyers time to review the case file. Abbas al-Maliki, a court-appointed lawyer representing one of the defendants, told Reuters his client was being tried on charges of membership of Islamic State. Islamic State seized large tracts of Syria and Iraq in 2014 before it was driven out by US-led coalition forces five years later. Many of the group's militants were detained, though remnants of the jihadist group still operate. The United States announced in January that it had begun [USN:L1N3YN16J TEXT:"transferring"] Islamic State detainees from Syria to Iraq amid concerns over the security of detention facilities in northeast Syria after Kurdish-led forces lost control of parts of the region. Iraq's Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said in February that [USN:L8N3Z90O1 TEXT:"discussions"] were being held with other countries to repatriate their citizens and that Baghdad had sought international financial support to deal with the influx of prisoners.

item.title: Top 25 roundup: Kenny Minchey leads Kentucky to upset of No. 9 Texas A&M
item.description: Kenny Minchey threw a pair of touchdown passes and CJ Baxter ran for two more as Kentucky scored a major upset with a 31-21 Southeastern Conference victory against No. 9 Texas A&M on Saturday at College Station, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kenny Minchey threw a pair of touchdown passes and CJ Baxter ran for two more as Kentucky scored a major upset with a 31-21 Southeastern Conference victory against No. 9 Texas A&M on Saturday at College Station, Texas. Kentucky (2-1, 1-1 SEC) beat Texas A&M (2-1, 0-1) for the first time since Oct. 4, 1952, though the teams have met just four times. Texas A&M suffered its first regular-season home loss since Nov. 2, 2024 against South Carolina. The Aggies also lost to Miami at home in the first round of the College Football Playoff last season. Minchey completed 14 of 18 passes for 252 yards and connected on his first nine passes in the second half for 142 yards. Texas A&M quarterback Marcel Reed ran for 80 yards and a touchdown and completed 26 of 49 passes for 236 yards and a touchdown. But Kentucky's defense, under the direction of former Texas A&M defensive coordinator Jay Bateman, intercepted Reed twice. No. 1 Texas 30, UTSA 6 Arch Manning threw two first-half touchdown passes to Cam Coleman and Gianni Spetic hit three field goals as the Longhorns sleepwalked through a victory over the Roadrunners in Austin, Texas, to conclude a three-game, season-opening homestand. Texas (3-0) but sputtered throughout, looking little like the team that roared back in the fourth quarter to beat then-No. 1 Ohio State on Sept. 12 to ascend to the top of the Associated Press rankings. Manning finished 16 of 32 for 161 yards and ran for 50 more. The Longhorns defense was the difference as UTSA (2-1) managed just 143 yards. Texas finished with more rushing yards (228) than the Roadrunners' total output. Owen McCown passed for 70 yards for UTSA, which was flagged for 12 penalties for 119 yards. No. 2 Georgia 45, Arkansas 17 Chauncey Bowens rushed for a career-high three touchdowns and the Bulldogs held the Razorbacks to 17 rushing yards in a win in Fayetteville, Ark. Gunner Stockton completed 10 of 13 passes for 147 yards and a touchdown and rushed for a team-high 97 yards for Georgia (3-0, 1-0 SEC), which improved to 11-0 in SEC road openers under head coach Kirby Smart. Nate Frazier rushed 14 times for 75 yards and a touchdown and Craig Dandridge Jr. had a 61-yard touchdown reception. KJ Jackson threw for 212 yards and a touchdown for Arkansas (1-2, 0-1), which dropped its 12th straight conference game. No. 3 Notre Dame 27, Michigan State 10 Micah Gilbert had eight catches for 170 yards and the Fighting Irish pulled away from the Spartans, who failed to score in the second half in South Bend, Ind. CJ Carr completed 18 of 24 passes for 234 yards and scored a touchdown on the ground for Notre Dame (3-0). Nolan James Jr. had 26 carries for 121 yards and a score. The Fighting Irish outgained the Spartans 395-167, holding the visitors to only 44 rushing yards. Alessio Milivojevic completed nine of 17 passes for 123 yards and tossed two interceptions for Michigan State (2-1). Reserve quarterback Cam Fancher rushed for the Spartans' lone touchdown. No. 4 Indiana 38, Western Kentucky 0 Josh Hoover threw for two touchdowns and Lee Beebe Jr. rushed for two as the Hoosiers pulled away for a nonconference win over the Hilltoppers in Bloomington, Ind. Hoover hit 18 of 24 passes for 273 yards, while Turbo Richard rushed for 149 yards and a score as Indiana (3-0) extended its winning streak to 19 games. The defense posted its second consecutive shutout while limiting Western Kentucky (0-3) to 186 yards. Florida State transfer Brock Glenn got his first start at quarterback for the Hilltoppers and completed 17 of 32 passes for 120 yards. He also rushed 11 times for a team-high 30 yards. No. 6 Ohio State 59, Kent State 3 The Buckeyes took out their frustrations on the Golden Flashes after a stunning defeat last week to Texas, as Julian Sayin passed for 241 yards and two touchdowns and receiver Jeremiah Smith had a record-setting day in Columbus, Ohio. Ohio State (2-1) rebounded from squandering a 20-point fourth-quarter lead during a 24-23 loss at now-No. 1 Texas last Saturday. Smith made five catches for 85, all in the first half, and set the Buckeyes' career receiving yards record. The junior entered needing 26 yards to surpass the 2,898 yards Michael Jenkins amassed in 38 games from 2001-03. Smith has 2,958 yards in 32 games. Kent State (1-2) was outgained 527-134 -- 382-63 through the air and 145-71 on the ground. Sean Leonard kicked a 30-yard field goal with 1:56 left in regulation for the final score of the game. No. 8 Ole Miss 32, No. 7 LSU 24 Trinidad Chambliss passed for two touchdowns and ran for a tiebreaking score in the fourth quarter as the Rebels held off the Tigers in Oxford, Miss. Chambliss completed 33 of 48 passes for 363 yards and had one interception. Ole Miss (3-0, 1-0 SEC) squandered a 17-point halftime lead before regaining control to defeat former Rebels head coach Lane Kiffin. Traylor Ray caught seven passes for 115 yards and a score. Sam Leavitt passed for 158 yards with a touchdown and an interception for LSU (2-1, 0-1). He also rushed for a TD, and Dilin Jones had 23 carries for 106 yards and a score. The Tigers drove to the Ole Miss 6, but on fourth and goal, Leavitt was intercepted by Jaylon Braxton with 58 seconds left in the game. No. 10 Alabama 50, Florida State 36 Keelon Russell threw three touchdown passes and ran for another score as the Crimson Tide overcame a pair of lightning delays and a slow start to rally past the Seminoles in Tuscaloosa, Ala. Russell completed 23 of 30 passes for 320 yards and added 56 yards on three carries. Lotzeir Brooks had eight catches for a career-high 101 yards for the Crimson Tide (3-0), who averaged 8.6 yards per play and scored nine straight times they touched the ball. Florida State (1-2) got a productive performance from quarterback Ashton Daniels, who threw for 377 yards and two scores while also tallying two rushing touchdowns. However, he was intercepted three times. Duce Robinson had six catches for 135 yards and a touchdown while Ousmane Kromah had 17 carries for 80 yards. No. 11 BYU 41, Colorado State 23 LJ Martin rushed for 176 yards and three touchdowns, and Bear Bachmeier completed 12 of 16 passes for 227 yards and an interception as the Cougars downed the Rams in Fort Collins, Colo. Freshman wide receiver Legend Glasker caught five passes for 131 yards and also rushed for a touchdown, and Preston Rex had a rushing score for BYU (3-0). The Cougars racked up a 559-302 advantage in total yards. Colorado State quarterback Hauss Hejny connected on 6 of 10 passing attempts for 80 yards and a touchdown but left the game in the first quarter with a hamstring injury. Backup quarterback K'saan Farrar threw for 70 yards and an interception. No. 3 quarterback Darius Curry passed for 70 yards and a touchdown for the Rams (2-1). No. 12 USC 42, Rutgers 35 Jayden Maiava threw for 277 yards and two touchdowns to help lift the Trojans to a Big Ten win over the Scarlet Knights in Piscataway, N.J. USC outgained Rutgers 461-460 in the game, including 184-168 on the ground. King Miller ran for 102 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries. Antwan Raymond led Rutgers with 122 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries, including a 49-yard carry to set up Clay Thevenin's touchdown. Rutgers (0-3, 0-1) outgained USC 289-209 in the second half, but never took the lead. Turnovers were costly for the Scarlet Knights. No. 14 Penn State 55, Buffalo 13 Koby Howard and James Peoples each scored two touchdowns as the Nittany Lions rolled over the Bulls in University Park, Penn. Rocco Becht threw for 212 yards and two touchdowns for the Nittany Lions (3-0), who outgained the Bulls 573-173. Penn State went just 2-for-10 on third downs, but Buffalo was even worse at 1-for-15. The Bulls (1-2) didn't score a touchdown until the fourth quarter, when James McNeil Jr. (20 carries for 80 yards) plunged into the end zone. Jason Wright went 10-for-25 for only 60 yards for Buffalo. No. 15 Tennessee 42, Kennesaw State 9 Daune Morris rushed for a career-high 116 yards and scored one touchdown to help the Volunteers clobber the Owls at Knoxville, Tenn. Faizon Brandon completed 18 of 26 passes for 178 yards and one touchdown for Tennessee (3-0). Brandon also rushed for 47 yards and one score. DeSean Bishop and Hunter Barnes also rushed for scores and Braylon Staley had a TD reception for the Vols, who had 268 rushing yards and outgained Kennesaw State 446-291. Daniel Kinney kicked three field goals for the Owls (1-2). Rickie Collins was 22-of-34 passing for 189 yards and Zion Booker had 10 catches for 78 yards. No. 17 Utah 33, Utah State 0 Devon Dampier threw for 253 yards and two touchdowns to lead the Utes to a shutout of the Aggies in Salt Lake City. Braden Pegan had a season-high 122 yards and two touchdowns on a season-high eight catches for Utah (3-0). Daniel Bray added 82 yards and another touchdown on three carries as the Utes rolled up 480 total yards. Nothing went right for Utah State (0-3) on either side of the ball. The Aggies gained only 10 first downs on the day to 23 for their opponent. Grady Brosterhous threw for 130 yards and had an interception. The Aggies tallied only 58 yards on the ground. No. 18 Iowa 55, Northern Iowa 0 Xavier Williams rushed for career highs of 151 yards and three touchdowns on just six carries to help the Hawkeyes steamroll the visiting Panthers at Iowa City, Iowa. Braeden Jackson also had a career day with 125 yards on 11 carries to go with two touchdowns (one rushing, one receiving). Nathan McNeil added career bests of 111 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 12 attempts for the Hawkeyes (3-0). Hank Brown made his third straight start for the Hawkeyes and completed all 12 of his passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns. Jaxon Dailey was 11-of-27 passing for 91 yards and two interceptions for Northern Iowa (1-2). The Panthers were 3-of-15 on third-down conversions. No. 19 Michigan 52, UTEP 17 Bryce Underwood passed for 223 yards and two touchdowns and the Wolverines scored four third-quarter touchdowns to roll past the Miners at Ann Arbor, Mich. Savion Hiter rushed for 62 yards and two scores on 11 carries, while Jordan Marshall had 59 yards and one touchdown on 12 carries. Andrew Marsh caught 10 passes for 105 yards and a touchdown, while JJ Buchanan had seven receptions for 92 yards and a score for Michigan (3-0). The Miners' EJ Colson Jr. passed for two touchdowns but also had an interception returned for a touchdown. UTEP (1-2) cashed in on a pair of Wolverines turnovers in the first half as Michigan headed to the locker room clinging to a 17-14 lead. No. 20 Missouri 27, Troy 17 Jamal Roberts rushed for 122 yards and a touchdown, and DaMarion Fowlkes scored on a 68-yard punt return to lead the Tigers to a victory against the visiting Trojans Columbia, Mo. Missouri (3-0) forced a pair of Troy turnovers and converted them into touchdowns in a 24-point second quarter, and the Tigers pitched a shutout on defense in the second half. Troy (2-1) scored the first 10 points of the game, kept Missouri off the scoreboard in the first quarter, and trailed by only a touchdown early in the fourth. Goose Crowder threw for 230 yards and two touchdowns, including a 76-yard score to TK Keyes on the second play of the Trojans' opening possession. No. 23 Louisville 41, No. 16 SMU 31 Keyjuan Brown rushed for 163 yards with two touchdowns, Isaac Brown had a crucial rushing score late and the Cardinals opened Atlantic Coast Conference play with home win over the a 41-31 home victory over the Mustangs. Keyjuan Brown went back and forth with SMU running back Kendrick Raphael, who had a career day with 197 yards on 24 attempts and three touchdowns. Lincoln Kienholz completed 14 of 23 passes for 177 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for 42 yards on 12 carries and a score for Louisville (2-1, 1-0 ACC). Kaleb Beasley recorded two interceptions, the second to seal the game with 1:31 left. Kevin Jennings was 24 of 35 for 222 yards and a touchdown, but he threw those two interceptions as SMU (2-1, 1-1) lost the turnover battle 3-0. No. 24 Oklahoma 14, New Mexico 6 John Mateer threw for 238 yards and two touchdowns as the Sooners avoided an upset with a win over the Lobos in Norman, Okla. The Sooners led 7-6 at the half, but stretched the lead on Isaiah Sategna's 53-yard touchdown catch midway through the third quarter, then the defense held off the Lobos. Oklahoma (2-1) outgained New Mexico (2-1) 299-185. Neither team could run effectively, combining for 130 yards. A trio of New Mexico quarterbacks combined to go for 8 of 19 for 116 yards. Cade Keith led the Lobos with five catches for 78 yards. Only two other players caught passes for New Mexico. West Virginia 38, No. 25 Virginia 27 Michael Hawkins Jr. ran for three touchdowns and threw two touchdown passes to fuel the Mountaineers' upset of the Cavaliers in the Duke's Mayo Classic in Charlotte, N.C. Hawkins completed 10 of 17 passes for 190 yards and rushed 18 times for a career-high 123 yards. DJ Epps had three receptions for 92 yards and two TDs, and Cam Cook added 123 yards on 30 carries as the Mountaineers improved to 3-0 for the first time since 2018. Jekail Middlebrook rushed for 75 yards and scored rushing and receiving TDs for the Cavaliers (2-1), who led 14-7 after the first quarter. Beau Pribula completed 21 of 33 passes for 197 yards and two touchdowns. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ten lions found dead in suspected poisoning at Tanzania wildlife reserve
item.description: Ten lions were found dead in Tanzania's Ngorongoro wildlife reserve this week and preliminary findings suggest they may have been poisoned, the area's management authority said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ten lions were found dead in Tanzania's Ngorongoro wildlife reserve this week and preliminary findings suggest they may have been poisoned, the area's management authority said. The deaths raise concerns over the conservation of lions in one of Africa's most renowned wildlife ecosystems. Poisoning has been a recurring threat to large carnivores across parts of East Africa, often linked to conflicts between predators and livestock owners. The lions were discovered on September 18 in the Ndutu area of Endulen Ward in Arusha region, the Ngorongoro Conservation Area Authority said in a statement released late on Saturday. "Preliminary findings suggest the animals may have died after ingesting poison," the authority said, adding that it had launched an investigation to determine the cause and identify those responsible. The Ngorongoro Conservation Area, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in northern Tanzania, is one of the country's leading tourism attractions. It is home to a wide range of wildlife, including lions, elephants, buffaloes and endangered black rhinos. Last month, police [USN:L8N44L0D7 TEXT:"arrested"] four suspects in an investigation into the deaths of 18 elephants across the border in Kenya.

item.title: Olympic dreams flicker as teqball awards first Asian Games medals
item.description: With Spanish soccer great Carles Puyol on board and a growing fan base in Asia, teqball's ambitious global federation is confident that the sport's quirky hybrid of soccer and table tennis will one day muscle its way on to the Olympic programme.
item.dc:creator: Ian Ransom
item.content:encoded: With Spanish soccer great Carles Puyol on board and a growing fan base in Asia, teqball's ambitious global federation is confident that the sport's quirky hybrid of soccer and table tennis will one day muscle its way on to the Olympic programme. Teqball took a small but firm step toward legitimacy on Sunday when it awarded its first Asian Games medals on its debut at the multi-sport event in Nagoya, with Thai athletes claiming three of the five titles. With capacity for only a few hundred fans, the Higashi Sports Centre was hardly Wembley Stadium but the crowd were impressed by the athletes' skill as they hoofed the ball back and forth across the sport's signature curved table. "It's an amazing milestone on our journey because the teq world community globally is dreaming of becoming an Olympic sport one day," International Teqball Federation (ITF) general secretary Laszlo Vajda told Reuters at the venue. "I'm very confident actually that our debut as a medal sport at the Asian Games will be such an event that the IOC (International Olympic Committee) will recognise that yes, the sport, the venue, the engagement, the reach, the relevance to young people, the attraction and all that is in place." HUNGARIAN ROOTS Teqball has roots in a training exercise during the golden era of Hungarian soccer in the mid-20th century when players practised "foot-tennis" across a net with a leather ball. The modern game has come a long way in a short time. It was conceived a little over a decade ago by two Hungarian friends, a former professional soccer player and a computer scientist, who played around with a soccer ball on a ping pong table. After refining the table's curve, the duo teamed up with a Hungarian businessman and set about popularising the sport. The ITF was set up in 2017 and has staged several world championships. For the uninitiated, the sport might appear a bit zany but it is in good company on an Asian Games programme laden with off-beat disciplines such as virtual taekwondo and esports. Many of them, like teqball, dream of a spot on the Olympics, which means legitimacy, funding and the chance to grow a global fan base. Teqball is still early on that journey and has been building its social media profile with the help of former soccer names such as ex-Barcelona captain Puyol, who played 100 times for Spain.
