Guterres has said that AI will be a major topic, adding that countries pushing its frontiers should set up "common guardrails in order to avoid this race to the bottom that could lead one day to a gigantic disaster at the global level." The secretary-general has long proposed global governance of AI. In 2023, the UN created an advisory body on the technology, with members including tech executives, government officials and academics. The warning has put Guterres at odds with Trump, who dismissed AI risks as a "hoax," saying there is a "sick conspiracy" against it and that China would benefit from the doubt being cast on its development. MIDDLE EAST ESCALATION The Middle East will again be a focus of discussions, as the [USN:FWN4580MR TEXT:"US-Israeli war on Iran"] continues to drive global inflation and destabilize the region. Recent gains by Houthi militants threaten shipping in the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait and could further spike energy prices. "It's very difficult to have a military solution for that problem, and the experience of fighting in Yemen demonstrated how complicated it is to have successful interventions," said Guterres, adding that the UN's envoy on Yemen was making a "huge effort" to advance talks. Peace talks remain stalled, however, as Iran and the US continue to exchange strikes and Trump threatens a major escalation of the war. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to address the assembly on Wednesday. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu – wanted by the International Criminal Court over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza that Israel denies – is to speak on Thursday. Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas will for the second year running not be at the gathering in person. The US, a close Israeli ally, again denied him a visa. On Thursday, the General Assembly voted to allow Abbas to appear via video. There is likely to be a high-level meeting on the [USN:L6N40Y0KB TEXT:"conflict in Sudan"] on the sidelines, diplomats said, although a diplomatic breakthrough is unlikely. UKRAINE, FOOD SECURITY Also on the agenda is Russia's more than four-year-old war in Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov will address the General Assembly. Zelenskiy will likely seek to shore up Ukraine's position ahead of what is expected to be another tough winter, diplomats said. The Security Council has been unable to take action to end the conflict because permanent member Russia holds a veto. Trump has at times appeared frustrated that he has been unable to broker an end to the war, a goal he declared a priority when he began his second term in January last year. The US president spoke with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin earlier this month, but it was unclear whether he plans to meet Zelenskiy in New York. Guterres highlighted the impact the war was having on civilians but also on food security and energy prices. "The effective blockade existing in the Black Sea is creating enormous problems that add to the problems generated by the Middle East crisis, and I think it would be very important to find a way to allow Ukrainian exports and Russian exports of food, fertilizers and energy to take place in a safe way through the Black Sea," he said.

item.title: Rookie Ethan Salas lifts Padres past Marlins in 10 innings
item.description: Rookie Ethan Salas stroked an RBI single in the bottom of the 10th inning Saturday night and the San Diego Padres edged the visiting Miami Marlins 7-6.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rookie Ethan Salas stroked an RBI single in the bottom of the 10th inning Saturday night and the San Diego Padres edged the visiting Miami Marlins 7-6. Salas' hit scored Jake Cronenworth, who started the inning as the automatic runner at second base and advanced to third on a wild pitch by Josh Ekness (2-4). After Sung-Mun Song fanned, Salas batted for Freddy Fermin and grounded a 0-2 fastball up the middle for San Diego's 11th walk-off win of the year. David Morgan (4-1) stranded runners at first and second in the top of the 10th to earn the win, San Diego's 12th in 13 games. The Padres tied the Chicago Cubs for the top wild-card spot in the National League at 86-69, a game ahead of Philadelphia, and reduced their magic number for clinching a playoff spot to three. Miami (76-79) forced extra innings when pinch hitter Griffin Conine pulled a 102 mph fastball from closer Mason Miller for a game-tying homer with one out in the ninth. It was Conine's 17th homer of the year. Both starters did not factor into the decision after rough outings. Miami right-hander Eury Perez permitted five runs on eight hits and three walks in 4 2/3 innings, whiffing four. San Diego righty Casey Mize lasted only three innings, allowing five hits and five runs while walking five and striking out two. The Marlins initiated scoring with three runs in the second. Joe Mack's fielder's choice scored Jakob Marsee, and Otto Lopez cracked a two-run homer over the left field wall, his 11th of the year. Samad Taylor got the Padres on the board in their half of the second with his second homer of the season, a 388-foot shot to left. But Miami upped the lead to 5-1 in the third as Agustin Ramirez grounded an RBI double down the left field line and scored on Esteury Ruiz's single. San Diego rallied for three runs in the third. Cronenworth coaxed a bases-loaded walk and Ty France scored on a balk by Perez, followed by a sacrifice fly by Taylor. Fernando Tatis Jr. drew the Padres even at 5-5 in the fourth when he rifled a leadoff homer an estimated 410 feet to right-center, his 24th of the year. They took the lead in the sixth when France ripped a two-out double just over the head of Ruiz in right, scoring Dustin Harris. --Field Level Media

item.title: Dernier jour des élections législatives en Russie
item.description: Les élections législatives en Russie, présentées par le président Vladimir Poutine comme un baromètre du soutien à la guerre contre l'Ukraine, sont entrées dimanche dans leur troisième et dernier jour.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les élections législatives en Russie, présentées par le président Vladimir Poutine comme un baromètre du soutien à la guerre contre l'Ukraine, sont entrées dimanche dans leur troisième et dernier jour. Le parti au pouvoir, "Russie unie", devrait conserver sa position dominante au sein d'un système politique qui, selon ses détracteurs, ne tolère pas la dissidence. Le scrutin, qui vise à renouveler les 450 sièges de la chambre basse du Parlement, la Douma d'Etat, est le premier organisé depuis que la Russie a lancé son invasion à grande échelle en Ukraine en février 2022. La plupart des candidats opposés à la guerre ont été exclus du scrutin après que la Cour suprême a jugé que le parti libéral Iabloko, qui réclame un cessez-le-feu en Ukraine, avait enfreint les règles électorales. Certains de ses candidats se sont toutefois présentés dans certaines circonscriptions. Le Kremlin affirme que l'unité nationale et une certaine censure sont nécessaires pendant la guerre en Ukraine, qu'il qualifie d'opération militaire spéciale. Vladimir Poutine a accusé vendredi l'Ukraine d'[USN:L6N45A196 TEXT:"ingérence"] dans les élections, citant en exemple une frappe ukrainienne ayant récemment touché un village situé dans une zone de Zaporijjia occupée par la Russie, tuant une responsable au sein de la commission électorale locale. Les autorités russes ont par ailleurs signalé samedi une [USN:L8N45B03A TEXT:"cyberattaque"] contre les systèmes de vote en ligne à Moscou. Les premiers résultats devraient commencer à être communiqués vers 18h00 GMT dimanche, les résultats complets étant attendus lundi.

item.title: Van dominates Pantoja to retain flyweight belt in UFC 331
item.description: Joshua Van put on a striking masterclass to secure a unanimous decision win over Alexandre Pantoja to retain his flyweight title in UFC 331 in Los Angeles, as the 24-year-old from Myanmar settled the score with the former champion after their first fight ended with a freak injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Joshua Van put on a striking masterclass to secure a unanimous decision win over Alexandre Pantoja to retain his flyweight title in UFC 331 in Los Angeles, as the 24-year-old from Myanmar settled the score with the former champion after their first fight ended with a freak injury. Pantoja had suffered an [USN:L6N3XD00V TEXT:"accidental elbow dislocation"] 26 seconds into their first fight in December last year, resulting in Van becoming the UFC flyweight champion without an outright win over the Brazilian, who had reigned over the division for over two years. Van, the first UFC champion from Myanmar, defended the belt against Tatsuro Taira in May but was left waiting until Saturday to seal his status as the best in the division as 36-year-old Pantoja recovered from the injury. "A lot of people said that was an accidental win... well, doubt me now," said Joshua after his second title defence that extended his professional MMA record to 18 wins and two losses. Pantoja took Van down in the first round, before landing heavy punches and knees in a fiery exchange, as Van retaliated with a slicing elbow. "You're too good to brawl with this guy," Van's coaches told him during the break, suggesting a more tactical approach. Van peppered Pantoja with left-handed jabs in the second round, and rocked the Brazilian with a fluid combination of punches in the third. Pantoja controlled the fourth round as he took Van down but was unable to submit him. In the final round, Van stalked Pantoja and knocked him down with an overhand right, securing the win in the judges' scorecards. In the co-main event, Armenian contender Arman Tsarukyan staked his claim for a shot at the lightweight title when he pinned Maurício Ruffy to the cage, rocked him with a left elbow and knocked him out with a right elbow with four seconds to spare in the first round. "I knew my time would come, so I was patient," said Tsarukyan, who extended his win streak to six fights, as he called for a bout with champion Justin Gaethje.

item.title: Malaysian ex-PM Najib working on conditions to start house arrest, his lawyers say
item.description: Malaysia's jailed former prime minister, Najib Razak, is working to fulfil the conditions to leave jail and begin his house arrest, including paying a 50-million-ringgit ($12-million) fine, his lawyers said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Malaysia's jailed former prime minister, Najib Razak, is working to fulfil the conditions to leave jail and begin his [USN:L6N45A03A TEXT:"house arrest"], including paying a 50-million-ringgit ($12-million) fine, his lawyers said on Sunday. Najib's ability to satisfy the condition "do not lie in his own hands" as a significant part of his assets, bank accounts and properties remain subject to freeze orders and enforcement proceedings by the government, the lawyers said in a statement. Najib, prime minister from 2009 to 2018, was found guilty of corruption in relation to the [USN:L6N3XT06B TEXT:"embezzlement"] of billions of dollars tied to 1Malaysia Development Berhad, a state investment fund he co-founded while in power. He has consistently denied wrongdoing. Malaysia's king agreed on Friday to let Najib Razak leave jail and serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. It was the second royal pardon over his conviction for his involvement in a multi-billion-dollar financial scandal. Malaysia's Prisons Department said in a statement on Sunday that it and the home affairs ministry were waiting for official written confirmation of the pardon before taking any action. By law, the home affairs minister has the power to gazette any premises as a prison, which could be used to designate Najib’s home as a place to serve his sentence. Najib has been "deeply moved" by the support he has received from the public, the lawyers said. The president of Najib's UMNO party, Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, said on Friday that a collection fund would be launched for party members and supporters to help Najib pay for the fine. The party had raised almost 1 million ringgit by Saturday noon, local media reported. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's multi-party government, which includes the DAP as well as Najib’s UMNO, has seen growing rifts over the government's response to issues of corruption.

item.title: Macron va rencontrer Carney à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon
item.description: Emmanuel Macron rencontrera dimanche le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, quelques semaines après que le président américain Donald Trump a publié sur les réseaux sociaux une image montrant l’archipel recouvert du drapeau américain.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Emmanuel Macron rencontrera dimanche le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, quelques semaines après que le président américain Donald Trump a publié sur les réseaux sociaux une image montrant l’archipel recouvert du drapeau américain. Cette visite, la première d'un président français depuis celle effectuée par François Hollande en 2014, intervient alors que le Canada cherche à renforcer ses liens avec l'Union européenne dans un contexte de tensions commerciales avec les Etats-Unis et de détérioration des relations avec Washington. A son arrivée dans l'archipel samedi soir, Emmanuel Macron a rappelé que Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon restait un territoire français. "C'est une évidence pour nous que c'est un territoire français, et un territoire attaché à la France et fier d'être français", a dit aux journalistes le chef de l'Etat. "Nous y sommes attachés. Il n'y a pas de débat, il n'y a pas de discussion." Un responsable de la présidence française avait déclaré plus tôt à la presse: "Pour un territoire de 5.800 habitants, il est rare de trouver autant d'enjeux importants pour la France concentrés dans un espace de cette taille: la présence géostratégique de la France dans l'Atlantique Nord, aux portes des Etats-Unis et de l'Arctique, la souveraineté maritime, l'adaptation au changement climatique, ainsi que la coopération avec le Canada." Selon des diplomates, cette visite, qu'Emmanuel Macron effectue avant de se rendre à l'Assemblée générale des Nations unies à New York, revêt une importance symbolique, après que Donald Trump a publié une carte représentant les Etats-Unis, le Canada, le Groenland, l'Islande, le Mexique, l'Amérique centrale et les Caraïbes enveloppés dans le drapeau américain et portant la mention "Etats-Unis d'Amérique". L'image incluait Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon ainsi que plusieurs territoires français des Caraïbes. La France avait alors choisi de ne pas réagir publiquement à cette publication. Emmanuel Macron et Mark Carney devraient aborder la crise énergétique ainsi que les relations de plus en plus étroites entre le Canada et l'UE, après que celle-ci a ouvert la voie à une adhésion d'Ottawa en tant que premier membre associé.

item.title: Mookie Betts, Dodgers stay hot in romp over Giants
item.description: Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and the Los Angeles Dodgers stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a 10-4 victory over the visiting San Francisco Giants on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and the Los Angeles Dodgers stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a 10-4 victory over the visiting San Francisco Giants on Saturday. Betts has 10 hits over his past three games, including seven in the past two while operating out of the leadoff spot in place of an injured Shohei Ohtani. Will Smith hit a home run as the Dodgers (95-60) won for the fifth time in six games and improved to 13-3 since Sept. 3. Tarik Skubal (11-7) gave up four runs on eight hits over five innings with three strikeouts. The left-hander is now 4-2 with a 2.85 ERA in nine starts for Los Angeles after a trade from the Detroit Tigers on Aug. 2. Victor Bericoto hit a home run among his two hits for the Giants (64-91) while Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings in his fourth career appearance and second start. San Francisco lost for the sixth time in its past eight games in its next-to-last road game of the season. Max Muncy had an RBI double in the first inning to score Betts as the Dodgers started a stretch in which they scored in each of the first six innings. Betts had an RBI single in the second. The Giants tied the score in the third on Bericoto's fifth home run over his first 35 career games. Los Angeles went back on top 3-2 in the third on Smith's leadoff home run. Both teams scored in the fourth, with San Francisco tying the score 4-4 in the fifth on a double from Jung Hoo Lee. Edman's two-run single in the fifth gave the Dodgers the lead for good and they added another in the inning for a 7-4 lead on a Miguel Rojas single. In the sixth, Smith added an RBI single, while rookie Josue De Paula followed with a two-run single for a 10-4 advantage. Los Angeles has a 5-4 advantage in the season series with four games still remaining between the teams. Smith went 3-for-5 as the Dodgers collected 15 hits. Lee went 2-for-4 for the Giants and drove in a run. The Giants had two hits in a dozen at-bats with runners in scoring position. --Field Level Media

item.title: Merz under pressure as two more German states go to the polls
item.description: The elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin follow the election in Saxony-Anhalt, where the far-right AfD came close to the rare feat of winning an absolute majority.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Denzer, Max Schwarz
item.content:encoded: German voters went to the polls on Sunday in two state elections that look likely to heap more pressure on struggling Chancellor Friedrich Merz, whose future has been [USN:L8N4571NP TEXT:"in the balance"] since the far right's triumph in another regional vote this month. The elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, a largely rural state in the formerly communist east, and the capital Berlin follow the [USN:L1N44Y01V TEXT:"September 6 election"] in Saxony-Anhalt, where the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) came close to the rare feat of winning an absolute majority. Polls were scheduled to close at 6 p.m. (1600 GMT), with the first exit polls expected soon after. Regional elections would not usually draw much interest outside Germany, but the AfD's success in Saxony-Anhalt, which it sees as the first step towards winning federal elections due in 2029, has sent shock waves through Europe. In just over a decade, the party, which wants to take tough action to deport foreigners with no right to stay in Germany, restore energy ties with Russia and quit the euro, has transformed itself from a fringe eurosceptic movement to the country's most popular party. Opinion polls indicate it is unlikely to repeat its victory in Saxony-Anhalt in either of Sunday's votes. But they are both expected to underscore the advances it has made in recent years and raise fresh questions over the "firewall" strategy, under which the other main parties refuse to enter coalition agreements with it. For Merz, whose approval ratings have plunged as low as 14%, according to the latest polls, the result was the most recent in a series of blows that have raised doubts in his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party about whether he can continue to lead. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the CDU looks likely to suffer its worst-ever election result, with the most recent opinion poll by the Forschungsgruppe Wahlen on Friday putting it at just 6% and at risk of failing to clear the minimum threshold to enter the state parliament. MERZ HAS STRUGGLED Elected last year on a promise of reforms to return Germany's stagnant economy to growth, Merz has struggled to win over voters, compounding resentment over unpopular pension, tax and healthcare reforms with a stream of communication missteps. For the moment at least, [USN:L8N4580EF TEXT:"senior CDU figures"] have rallied behind him, aware that replacing the chancellor - which would in any case be difficult on constitutional grounds - would leave any successor facing the same deep economic problems. But disillusion with his government has hung over the campaigns in both Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin, where voters have focused on issues including soaring energy and housing costs. Merz [USN:L8N45A15I TEXT:"presented"] a consumer relief package on Friday that included tax cuts on gas and diesel. Several people heading to vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania said living costs were a major concern. "Here in Schwerin, with these wages, you can hardly afford anything anymore," voter Carlotta Heick told Reuters in the state capital. One elderly man criticised funding for foreign aid. "We need our money here, for our country, for children and pensioners," he said, asking not to give his name. In the rural state, polls have shown the race narrowing over recent weeks as the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) have centred their campaign around popular [USN:L8N4571NP TEXT:"state premier Manuela Schwesig"]. The Wahlen poll on Friday showed the SPD edging in front of the AfD for the first time in months. The poll put the SPD on 37%, the AfD on 36%, the far-left Left Party on 9% and the environmental Greens on 5%, just at the threshold for entering parliament. Both parties would be potential coalition partners for Schwesig. At her closing campaign rally, Schwesig warned of "dark clouds" as she referred to the AfD, calling it a dangerous party. Wrapping up the AfD's campaign in the state, national party leader Alice Weidel took aim at Merz. "From next week, the chancellor's tone will become very quiet," she said, telling supporters they had the power to unseat him in Sunday's election. In Berlin, the Wahlen poll showed the far-left Left Party moving ahead of the CDU, threatening the conservative hold on the mayor's office. Even in liberal Berlin, however, the AfD has made strong gains, moving into third place. The poll put the Left Party on 22%, the CDU on 20%, the Greens on 15% and the SPD on 12%. The AfD sits on 18%, while the far-left BSW, the only party that has said it might work with the AfD, is just under the parliamentary threshold on 4%.

item.title: Pavin Smith’s pinch-hit, walk-off homer lifts D-backs over Yankees
item.description: Pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run, walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory over the Yankees.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run, walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory over the Yankees. Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 391-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece. Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six. The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the American League East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild-card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday. The D-backs (81-74) gained a game on Philadelphia (85-70) for the third spot in the National League wild-card race but are still four games back with seven games to play. Yankees starter and American League Cy Young candidate Cam Schlittler gave up three hits and three runs (one earned) in six innings, leaving when his pitch count reached 98. His season high is 106. Schlittler struck out three and walked six while lowering his ERA to an AL-leading 1.94. He has given up one earned run or fewer in each of his last eight starts. Arizona starter Brandon Pfaadt gave up four singles and one run in 4 1/3 innings, leaving after the Yankees loaded the bases on three singles in the fifth. Ben Rice hit a sacrifice fly off Justin Martinez to break a scoreless tie. Pfaadt struck out three and walked one. The D-backs broke up Schlittler's no-hitter with a two-run fifth. Both runs scored after Schlittler's one-out fielding error. Arenado had Arizona's first hit, a line single to left field with one out, before Tim Tawa pushed a bunt toward the mound. Schlittler could not field the ball cleanly and both runners were safe. Lawlar lined a two-out triple to left-center on a 99 mph fastball for a 2-1 lead. Ramos and Wells homered in the sixth to put the Yankees in front 3-2. The D-backs tied it in the sixth when Ketel Marte and Gabriel Moreno drew four-pitch walks and Geraldo Perdomo beat out a two-strike bunt single to load the bases. Corbin Carroll hit a sacrifice fly before Schlittler struck out Arenado and Tawa with runners on second and third. --Field Level Media

item.title: Macron and Carney to meet in French Atlantic archipelago in signal to Trump
item.description: President Emmanuel Macron arrived in the French territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon for talks with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Sunday, weeks after President Donald Trump posted an image showing the islands covered by the US flag.
item.dc:creator: John Irish
item.content:encoded: President Emmanuel Macron arrived in the French territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon for talks with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Sunday, weeks after President Donald Trump posted an image showing the islands covered by the US flag. Macron's visit to the archipelago off Canada's Atlantic coast is the first there by a French president since 2014 and comes as Canada seeks closer [USN:S8N4150LY TEXT:"ties with the European Union"] amid an increasingly acrimonious trade war with the United States. Saint Pierre and Miquelon is France's only remaining territory in North America, and French officials said Macron's trip would underscore French sovereignty and highlight close ties with Canada. "There's no doubt (it is French)," Macron said after landing in the territory of 5,800 inhabitants late on Saturday. "We are not going to affirm it every day because people have strange ideas or say strange things," he told reporters responding to a question on Trump's map. VISIT CARRIES SYMBOLIC WEIGHT Diplomats said the visit by Macron, who was en route to the annual United Nations General Assembly of world leaders, had a symbolic weight following Trump's social media post. The image Trump shared showed the US flag draped over the United States, Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean and was labelled "United States of America". It included Saint Pierre and Miquelon and French Caribbean territories. France did not respond publicly to the post at the time. For France, Saint Pierre and Miquelon is strategically important due to its location on the doorstep of the US and the Arctic, a French presidency official told reporters in a briefing ahead of the visit. The territory also occupies a key place in France's cooperation with Canada, including over energy, one of the issues in focus for the meeting on Sunday between Macron and Carney. Macron, whose government is facing increased pressure at home over rising fuel prices, said he would like Canada to broaden its exports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Europe rather than primarily Asia. The two leaders will also discuss Canada's ties with the EU after the bloc opened the door to Ottawa becoming its first associate member, diplomats said. Any move towards deeper integration is likely to face hurdles. More than a decade after the EU and Canada agreed the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, and nine years after its provisional application began, several EU member states have yet to ratify the accord, including France.

item.title: Ukraine launches biggest Moscow drone attack as Russia votes
item.description: The strikes killed two people in the Moscow region and two more in the Russian-held part of Ukraine's Kherson region, officials said. A facility at Moscow's oil refinery also sustained damage.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Osborn, Vladimir Soldatkin
item.content:encoded: Ukraine launched what Moscow's mayor called the biggest drone attack yet on the Russian capital on Sunday, as Russians voted on the final day of a [USN:L6N451112 TEXT:"parliamentary election"] that President Vladimir Putin has cast as a test of support for the war in Ukraine. The drone strikes killed [USN:L1N45C00L TEXT:"two people"] in the Moscow region and [USN:L6N45C01J TEXT:"two more"] in the Russian-held part of Ukraine's Kherson region, including an election official, according to Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin and election authorities. A [USN:FWN45A0G8 TEXT:"facility "]at Moscow's oil refinery, which has been targeted before, was also [USN:L8N45C01S TEXT:"damaged"]. "The biggest attack by enemy drones has been repelled," Sobyanin said on Telegram. "This unprecedented attack was clearly planned with the aim of disrupting the elections. The enemy did not succeed." The State Duma vote, the first since Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022, is expected to see the ruling United Russia party easily retain its dominance in a political system critics say does not tolerate dissent. The Kremlin i[USN:L6N45A0MN TEXT:"s likely to present"] the outcome as evidence of public backing for Putin's policies and for the war, now in its fifth year with no sign of ending soon. The election authorities say the three days of voting have proceeded smoothly despite [USN:L1N45B029 TEXT:"cyberattacks"] reported on Saturday. Turnout was at over 50% by early afternoon Moscow time, Interfax news agency reported, citing the Central Election Commission. Most anti-war candidates have been barred from the ballot. Those who did run from the liberal Yabloko party, which has polled in the single digits in recent years but hoped to tap into war fatigue, said they [USN:L6N4530O5 TEXT:"feared for their freedom"] after courts handed long jail terms to two senior party figures before the vote for comments about the conflict. Discrediting the army or spreading what authorities regard as fake news is punishable by lengthy prison sentences. In a small act of defiance, Yabloko's leader, Nikolai Rybakov, demonstrably spoiled his ballot paper, writing his party's name and the slogan "For peace". The Kremlin says national unity and some censorship are necessary during what it calls its special military operation in Ukraine. It casts the conflict - Europe's deadliest since World War Two - as part of an existential struggle with a hostile West. Moscow says Ukrainian intelligence services and other enemies are stepping up efforts to stir unrest inside Russia. PERMITTED OPPOSITION PARTIES COULD BENEFIT Russian electoral officials said on Saturday that an online voting system in Moscow [USN:L1N45B029 TEXT:"had come under cyberattack."] Kyiv, which has suspended elections under martial law, has dismissed the Russian vote as a "pseudo election". Putin on Friday also [USN:L1N45A0ZW TEXT:"accused Ukraine"] of trying to interfere in the election, citing what he said was a Ukrainian strike that killed an election official in her home in the Russian-controlled part of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region on Tuesday. Reuters could not independently verify details of the attack and there was no comment from Kyiv. Despite what experts see as the election's predictable outcome, the NEST think-tank in Berlin, co-founded by Kremlin critic Mikhail Khodorkovsky, whom Russian authorities have designated "a foreign agent", said the vote could still produce awkward moments for the Kremlin at a time of [USN:L8N456064 TEXT:"economic strain"]. "The consequences of the war are increasingly being felt within the country, and [USN:L6N44V10B TEXT:"accumulated anxiety and frustration"] may translate into votes for the systemic opposition parties that the Kremlin has allowed to remain on the ballot," it said in a note. It said the Communist party and the New People party could attract votes the authorities would prefer to go to United Russia. Both parties have consistently voted in line with United Russia on major issues. Putin told the nation [USN:S8N44V093 TEXT:"in a televised address"] before the election that the vote would underline support for Russian troops fighting in Ukraine. "Your choice, and your will, will once again demonstrate that millions of people stand behind our soldiers, that we are a united people bound together by shared values, historical memory, and love for our homeland, and that no one will succeed in dividing or intimidating us," said Putin. Initial results are expected to start emerging at around 1800 GMT on Sunday, with more complete results available on Monday.

item.title: China's CXMT says new memory-chip platform enters mass production
item.description: Chinese DRAM chipmaker CXMT said on Sunday its fifth-generation technology platform had entered mass production, a claimed breakthrough that could help China build a stronger competitor to Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology in the global market for memory chips.
item.dc:creator: Che Pan, Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: Chinese DRAM chipmaker CXMT (688825.SS) said on Sunday its fifth-generation technology platform had entered mass production, a claimed breakthrough that could help China build a stronger competitor to Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology in the global market for memory chips. DRAM, or dynamic random-access memory, is the short-term working memory that phones, computers and other devices use to run apps and programs. The new platform is designed to make more powerful memory chips at lower cost and with less power use. CXMT, which listed on Shanghai's STAR Market this year, said it would give electronics makers an additional source of supply for chips used in smartphones and other devices. CXMT, China's leading producer of DRAM, said the new platform packs the tiny structures that store data closer together, allowing more memory to fit on each chip and more individual chips to be made from each silicon wafer. The Hefei-based memory-chip maker said it had reduced the spacing of key features in the part of the chip that stores data to 11.95 nanometres, or about 12 billionths of a metre. It achieved this using "quadruple patterning," a process that repeats several manufacturing steps to produce finer circuit patterns. "Our process capability is now on par with the most advanced mass-produced nodes out there in the industry," Luo Xiaodong, CXMT's vice president and head of its marketing centre, said at the 2026 World Manufacturing Convention in Hefei. CXMT UNVEILS TWO NEW CHIPS CXMT also unveiled two 24-gigabit LPDDR5X products made on the new platform. LPDDR5X is a power-saving type of DRAM used mainly in smartphones and other portable electronics. The products each hold 50% more data than CXMT's previous equivalent products and are already in mass production, the company said. They are offered in two package formats for different smartphone and portable-device designs. CXMT said the platform can produce at least 50% more gross chip dies per wafer than its fourth-generation platform, using an 8-gigabit-chip baseline. That measures the potential number of chips made from a wafer before defective units are excluded, rather than the proportion that pass final testing. CXMT said it developed the platform using computer simulations and joint work with Chinese chip-equipment makers on critical production steps. The advance comes as Beijing seeks to reduce reliance on foreign semiconductor technology and US export controls since 2022 have restricted China's access to certain advanced chipmaking equipment and related software.

item.title: Nationals tally four in 11th; outlast struggling Cardinals
item.description: Jose Tena's two-run double keyed a four-run 11th inning and the Washington Nationals beat the Cardinals 8-5 on Saturday night in St. Louis.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jose Tena's two-run double keyed a four-run 11th inning and the Washington Nationals beat the Cardinals 8-5 on Saturday night in St. Louis. Keibert Ruiz singled leading off the 11th against Gordon Graceffo (8-2), moving designated runner Yohandy Morales to third. Nasim Nunez walked to load the bases and Jacob Young reached on a catcher's interference call against Leo Bernal, plating the go-ahead run. Daylen Lile struck out, but Tena smacked a double to left center and the lead expanded to 7-4. CJ Abrams was walked intentionally and Dylan Crews hit a sacrifice fly to right that would have been more damaging if not for a diving catch by Jordan Walker. JJ Wetherholt singled home a run leading off the bottom half against Riley Cornelio. Alec Burleson singled and Jose Fermin walked to load the bases. But Ivan Herrera and Jordan Walker struck out, and Will Dion came on, getting Bernal to fly out for his first major league save. Jorbit Vivas had four hits and Lile homered for Washington (73-82), which has won six of seven. Cornelio (3-2) pitched 1 2/3 innings for the win. At the top of the order, Fermin and Herrera had three hits each for St. Louis (75-80), which has lost four straight. Vivas singled home a run in the top of the 10th and Masyn Winn matched him in the bottom half. St. Louis tied it in the ninth. Nathan Church led off with a double to left and scored on Pedro Pages' single. Trailing 3-0, the Cardinals rallied in the seventh. Winn reached on a throwing error by third baseman Vivas and went to second on a ground out. Pages hit a dribbler toward third and pitcher Richard Lovelady threw wildly to first. Winn scored and Pages went to second. One out later Fermin singled, scoring Pages to make it 3-2. James Wood opened the game with a single and Lile followed with a two-run homer. The Nationals added a run in the sixth. Vivas singled with one out and Andres Chaparro followed with an infield hit. After Ruiz grounded into a fielder's choice, Nunez singled, scoring Vivas to make it 3-0. Washington's Andrew Alvarez tossed six shutout innings. He gave up five hits and tied his season high with eight strikeouts. Cardinals starter Michael McGreevy gave up two runs on five hits over four innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: IOC chief Coventry gives thumbs-up to Asian Games accommodation despite criticism
item.description: Several athletes have complained about cramped living quarters and undersized beds.
item.dc:creator: Ian Ransom
item.content:encoded: International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry threw her weight behind the beleaguered Asian Games organisers on Sunday, saying she was impressed with the athletes' accommodation in Nagoya despite criticism from some competitors. Japanese organisers scrapped initial plans for a [USN:L6N4590KW TEXT:"dedicated Athletes' Village"] in an effort to control costs, opting instead to house 17,000 athletes and officials across hotels, shipping-container-style huts and a cruise ship. Several athletes have complained about cramped living quarters and undersized beds, but Coventry gave the facilities a resounding thumbs-up after inspecting the accommodation at Garden Pier. "The cabins are quiet, they're very cool. The air conditioning is working well. The flooring and the walls are beautiful," Coventry told reporters afterwards. "It's better than some of the (athletes') villages I've ever stayed in. So I think to be very fair to Japan and to the organising committee, I was really impressed. "I'd only been reading everything that had been said, and I was expecting something completely different to when I walked in. And I hope that you guys will get to experience the same thing." Coventry, a former Olympic swimming champion, said this was not the first time athletes had been housed in such modular setups even though these were slightly smaller than the cabins used in Milano Cortina Winter Olympics earlier this year. "We had cabins in 2000, my very first (Olympic) Games in Australia. It's not a new concept. I'm not necessarily concerned about the look." The overarching priority remained ensuring that competitors enjoyed a positive overall experience, the Zimbabwean added. "I think what athletes expect from us is that there needs to be a minimum level of standards, right? And we're going to try and work with everybody to do that."

item.title: Trump seeks to bring health-research funding under his control, Politico reports
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump is seeking to bring a major part of national funding for health research under the control of his political appointees, Politico reported on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. President Donald Trump is seeking to bring a major part of national funding for health research under the control of his political appointees, Politico reported on Saturday. Trump has directed his budget director, Russ Vought, to draft an executive order to create a board that would decide which grants would be funded by the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the news outlet said, citing two administration officials familiar with the meeting. The board would include NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya and Vought, the director of the White House Office of Management and Budget, and would be required to reach unanimous decisions on grant awards, the report said. The proposed arrangement would give Vought a direct role in determining how the health research agency distributes its congressionally-appropriated money, the report added. The Office of Management and Budget, the White House and the Health and Human Services Department that oversees the NIH did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours. The reported move comes amid mounting criticism of the US government's research [USN:L1N3Y60VZ TEXT:"funding cuts"], undertaken last year to target federal spending at major universities, resulting in the freezing or cancellation of grants at numerous institutions. The Trump administration says these cuts are necessary to ensure the government funds only solid science and to reverse years of misguided priorities.

item.title: Rockies score 4 times in seventh to rally past Mariners
item.description: Cole Carrigg delivered a go-ahead two-run single in a four-run seventh inning as the Colorado Rockies edged the Seattle Mariners 5-3 on Saturday night in Denver.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Cole Carrigg delivered a go-ahead two-run single in a four-run seventh inning as the Colorado Rockies edged the Seattle Mariners 5-3 on Saturday night in Denver. Juan Mejia (4-6) pitched two scoreless innings and Brennan Bernardino got the final three outs for his second save for Colorado (57-98). Cal Raleigh and Randy Arozarena homered and Julio Rodriguez and Michael Arroyo had two hits each for Seattle (72-83), which is on the brink of elimination in the AL wild-card race. Before the game, the Rockies honored Hall of Fame first baseman Todd Helton with the unveiling of a statue in front of Coors Field. The statue depicts Helton celebrating after catching the last out of the 2007 NLCS that sent Colorado to the World Series. Colorado lefty Jose Quintana made his first start since May 24, missing nearly four months with a left elbow sprain. He allowed three runs on five hits in four innings and gave up two home runs. Raleigh gave the Mariners a 2-0 lead in the first with a two-run homer, his 23rd of the season, and Arozarena made it 3-0 in the third inning with his 26th long ball. But Colorado capitalized on bad Seattle defense to get a run back in the bottom of the inning. With one out, Jake McCarthy laid down a bunt single that Raleigh fielded and threw wildly to first, allowing McCarthy to advance to third. Connor Norby hit a fly ball to short right, and McCarthy raced home when Dominic Canzone's throw short-hopped Raleigh. That was all Seattle starter Bryce Miller gave up. He allowed an unearned run on four hits and struck out six in 5 1/3 innings. The Rockies rallied in the seventh to take the lead against reliever Jose Ferrer (4-4). Zac Veen and Adael Amador hit one-out singles and Veen came around on McCarthy's groundout. With two outs, Norby delivered an infield single, bringing up TJ Rumfield, who drove in Amador with a single up the middle to knot the game at 3-3. Hunter Goodman walked to load the bases and Carrigg hit a two-run single to center off Cooper Criswell to put Colorado in front. Norby and Rumfield each had a pair of singles for Colorado, which did not record an extra-base hit. --Field Level Media

item.title: Townsend hit by pitch roller while warming up in Thai league
item.description: Former England forward Andros Townsend was nearly run over by a motorised pitch roller while warming up with his Prachuap teammates at half-time during a Thai League 1 match on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former England forward Andros Townsend was nearly run over by a motorised pitch roller while warming up with his Prachuap teammates at half-time during a Thai League 1 match on Saturday. The 35-year-old avoided serious injury and later made a brief appearance in the match at Pattani. The former Tottenham Hotspur player did not see the roller, driven by a ground staff member, coming towards him when he stepped out of the practice area to attempt a pass. The roller knocked Townsend over and drove up his legs nearly to his waist before the driver jumped off and tried to lift it off the player. Townsend got back up and continued practicing, and came on as a late substitute while Prachuap cruised to a 3-0 victory. "Turns out Stoke away wasn't so bad after all," Townsend later wrote on Instagram, joking about the English side Stoke City's reputation as a tough place for visiting teams to play.

item.title: Japan win first gold of home Games, prodigy Yu leads China's pool surge
item.description: China wasted precious little time racing to a double-digit gold-medal haul.
item.dc:creator: Amlan Chakraborty
item.content:encoded: Hosts Japan won the first event of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Sunday, but China wasted precious little time racing to a double-digit gold-medal haul with teenage sensation Yu Zidi clinching the women's 200m butterfly title in Games record time. China's Olympic champion Pan Zhanle secured gold in the men's 100m freestyle. While his time of 47.61 seconds fell short of his own world record of 46.40, it was enough to successfully defend the crown he claimed in Hangzhou three years ago. “I was a little short of what I expected. I wanted to do better and swim faster but first of all I am happy to have won," Pan said. “This was my best result in the past two years. It was still below what I expected but I will take it step by step. I believe I can swim faster in the future.” TEQBALL MAKES GAMES DEBUT Pan relied on a late burst to edge a tight contest but Yu, who turns 14 next month, led end to end at the Tokyo Aquatics Centre to secure gold on her Asian Games debut, clocking two minutes, 5.08 seconds. Her effort eclipsed compatriot Zhang Yufei's previous mark of 2:05.57 set in Hangzhou, though rewriting the record books still left the prodigy hungry for more. "It was only so-so. I hope I can swim even faster. I improved my time by 0.9 seconds here and I believe I will perform better next time," she said. "My technique is still slightly lacking. I need to lower my head earlier, reach farther forward and improve the movement of my legs. Those are all areas that I need to work on." Thailand claimed three of the five gold medals on offer as teqball made its Asian Games debut — a milestone the sport's [USN:L6N45C01T TEXT:"governing body views"] as a crucial step toward its ultimate ambition of joining the Olympic programme. “I am so happy I could die right now," South Korean Lee Jun-suk said after winning the men's singles gold. "We just prepared for six months. We prepared really hard. I wanted to be a medallist but I didn’t imagine this situation.” PERFECT START FOR JAPAN Earlier in the day, hosts Japan enjoyed the perfect start when Takumi Hojo powered to victory in the men's individual triathlon in the first full day of competition. Hojo emerged from the warm waters of Mikawa Bay in fourth position and completed the cycling leg in fifth before pulling away on the run to win by nine seconds ahead of China's Zhang Xirui. Kazakhstan's Arlan Zhanabay crossed the line a further six seconds back to take bronze. "I was really fired up – even the rain held off, and I was in top form right up until I stood on the starting line," said Hojo, who won mixed relay gold at the Hangzhou Games. "I'd planned to attack using my strengths right until the end. "As it's our first gold medal, it's given the Japanese team a real boost and we've managed to pass the baton on to the women and our teammates for the relay." Following a build-up marred by athlete complaints over accommodation and logistics, organisers could take comfort as the spotlight finally shifted to sporting action. International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry [USN:L6N45C00K TEXT:"threw her weight behind"] the organisers on Sunday, saying she was impressed with the athletes' living quarters in Nagoya despite criticism from several competitors. Logistical hiccups lingered, however, with South Korea [USN:L6N45C01I TEXT:"complaining"] that their men's basketball team missed a scheduled practice session ahead of Sunday's final when their official shuttle bus failed to arrive.

item.title: Rangers stay hot, take down Blue Jays
item.description: The Texas Rangers won for the sixth time in their past seven games, defeating the Toronto Blue Jays 6-2 on Saturday in Arlington, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Texas Rangers won for the sixth time in their past seven games, defeating the Toronto Blue Jays 6-2 on Saturday in Arlington, Texas. Rangers starting pitcher Cal Quantrill left the game after 1 1/3 innings with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery (1-0) replaced him and held Toronto hitless through 3 2/3 innings. Jose Soriano (12-8) gave up six runs (five earned) on four hits and struck out eight in five-plus innings for the Blue Jays (76-79), who dropped to three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild-card berth in the American League. Josh Jung gave Texas (78-77) a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first with a home run to right field. The Rangers added two more runs despite not recording a hit in the second frame. Wyatt Langford drew a walk to lead off and, one out later, Nicky Lopez caught a pitch off his right foot. Langford came around to score on a fielder's choice when shortstop Andres Gimenez missed the throw to second base on Danny Jansen's grounder. Lopez, who advanced to third on Gimenez's error, scored on Soriano's wild pitch to make it 3-0. Toronto didn't get its first baserunner until the fourth inning on a walk to Vladimir Guerrero Jr., and it took until the sixth for its first hit, against Nathan Eovaldi. A curveball from Eovaldi caught Gimenez on the foot to lead off the sixth frame. Gimenez moved to second on Brett Bateman's one-out single, and Alejandro Kirk brought him in with a two-out base hit to center to cut it to 3-1. The hosts widened the gap in the bottom half. Jung was hit by a pitch, Brandon Nimmo singled and Langford's double off the left field wall scored Jung to push the advantage to 4-1. That ended Soriano's night, replaced by Paul Sewald. After striking out Jake Burger for the first out, Sewald intentionally walked Lopez to load the bases. He then hit Danny Jansen, forcing in Nimmo. Evan Carter then connected for a sacrifice fly that brought Langford home to extend it to 6-1. Toronto's Davis Schneider pinch-hit a solo shot to left center to narrow it to 6-2 in the seventh. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ronald Acuna Jr.’s late grand slam leads Braves past Astros
item.description: Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a grand slam, Grant Holmes produced a quality start, and the visiting Atlanta Braves lowered their magic number to one to clinch the National League East by defeating the Houston Astros 6-3 on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a grand slam, Grant Holmes produced a quality start, and the visiting Atlanta Braves lowered their magic number to one to clinch the National League East by defeating the Houston Astros 6-3 on Saturday. The Braves (91-64) secured this three-game interleague series and set the table to win the National League East for the seventh time in nine seasons with a victory in the series finale on Sunday. The Astros (77-78) fell below .500 for the first time since Aug. 26 and dropped a game behind the Texas Rangers in the American League West after Texas beat the Toronto Blue Jays 6-2. Isaac Paredes, who recorded both RBIs for the Astros in their 6-2 loss on Friday, homered with two outs in the bottom of the first inning off Holmes (10-5). The clout was his 22nd home run of the season and gave Houston a 1-0 lead. Two innings later, Paredes struck again. He flipped an RBI single to right with one out in the third, scoring Jeremy Pena. Pena had opened the frame with a triple to left-center. Holmes stranded runners in the first and second innings but settled down after Paredes doubled the Astros' lead to 2-0. Holmes retired the final two batters of the third and faced the minimum in the fourth and sixth despite allowing base hits in each frame. Holmes induced Yainer Diaz to ground into a double play, erasing a leadoff single by Jose Altuve in the bottom of the sixth. Holmes allowed two runs on eight hits and struck out four over six innings. Astros right-hander Hayden Wesneski appeared set to make the lead stand. He stranded runners on the corners in the top of the first and retired seven consecutive batters entering the sixth. But Drake Baldwin opened the sixth with a single. He scored two batters later when Matt Olson chased Wesneski with an RBI single. Acuna struck the decisive blow an inning later when he launched a fastball from Astros reliever Bryan Abreu 411 feet to left-center to give the Braves a 5-2 lead. Three of those runs were charged to Astros reliever AJ Blubaugh (5-3), who loaded the bases before Abreu entered with one out, struck out Baldwin, but allowed the two-out grand slam to Acuna. Acuna finished 2-for-3 with two walks. Closer Raisel Iglesias notched his 34th save for the Braves. Wesneski allowed one run on four hits with four strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings. Altuve went 3-for-4 for Houston. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brandon Lowe's 2-run homer lifts Pirates over Royals
item.description: Brandon Lowe launched a go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to power the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 6-5 victory over the visiting Kansas City Royals on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Brandon Lowe launched a go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to power the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 6-5 victory over the visiting Kansas City Royals on Saturday. Ronny Simon and Jake Mangum each hit two-run homers, while Oneil Cruz, Rafael Flores Jr. and Lowe each had two hits for the Pirates (78-77). Right-hander Luke Weaver (3-1) threw a scoreless eighth with one strikeout, and left-hander Mason Montgomery earned his 15th save of the season after working around a walk with one strikeout in a scoreless ninth. Nick Loftin had four hits, while Bobby Witt Jr. went 3-for-5 with two runs and extended his on-base streak to 17 games for the Royals (67-88). Carter Jensen hit a solo homer, while Jac Caglianone and Vinnie Pasquantino each had two hits for Kansas City. Flores led off the eighth by singling on a 0-2 pitch before Lowe homered off Royals reliever Steven Cruz (2-4) for his fourth blast in five games and 33rd of the season to give the Pirates a 6-5 lead. The Pirates had taken a 2-0 lead in the second inning when Simon hit his first career home run in 42 games, a two-run shot just inside the left field foul pole. In the third, Jensen set a Royals rookie record with his 25th home run of the season, trimming Pittsburgh's advantage to 2-1. Mangum's two-run homer in the fourth to left extended Pittsburgh's lead to 4-1. The Royals trimmed their deficit to 4-3 in the fifth. Witt legged out a slow roller to third, and after Caglianone walked, Pittsburgh starter Bubba Chandler was relieved by Brandon Eisert. Witt and Caglianone executed a double steal to put runners on second and third. Pasquantino's groundout plated Witt, and one batter later, Michael Massey's sacrifice bunt brought home Caglianone. Ryan O'Hearn made a slick glove flip through his legs to Eisert, who tagged first base just before a head-first sliding Massey. In the seventh, Kansas City collected four hits and scored two runs to take a 5-4 lead on RBI singles by Caglianone and Loftin. Royals starter Noah Cameron allowed four runs on seven hits with two walks and six strikeouts. Chandler yielded three runs on eight hits with a walk and six strikeouts.

item.title: Cubs come through in late innings, top Reds
item.description: Michael Busch and Dansby Swanson hit solo home runs to lift the visiting Chicago Cubs to a 5-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Michael Busch and Dansby Swanson hit solo home runs to lift the visiting Chicago Cubs to a 5-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Saturday. The win allowed the Cubs (86-69) to pull a full game ahead of the Philadelphia Phillies for the top wild-card playoff spot in the National League. The Phillies lost 10-3 to the Mets earlier in the day. The San Diego Padres (86-69) also won to remain tied with the Cubs. The Reds fell to 72-83. The teams will play the rubber game of the series Sunday. Cubs starter Matthew Boyd (9-5) gave up two hits and two runs (one earned) in five innings. The left-hander walked two and struck out four in 71 pitches. Ryan Rolison picked up his third save by getting the final out. Reds starter Nick Lodolo (3-6) gave up seven hits and three runs in seven innings. The left-hander walked two and struck out one in 90 pitches. The Cubs started the scoring in the second after Nico Hoerner led off with a double to center. Busch was hit by a pitch. Hoerner moved to third on a fielder's choice by Carson Kelly and scored on a deep sacrifice fly by Matt Shaw. Chicago made it 2-0 in the fifth after Swanson led off with an infield single. Swanson moved around to third on groundouts by Pete Crow-Armstrong and Alex Bregman and scored on a single to left by Seiya Suzuki. Boyd had allowed only a walk and had retired 11 straight before running into trouble in the fifth. Eugenio Suarez led off with a walk. JJ Bleday followed with a one-out single to right. Suarez headed to third on the play and shortstop Swanson uncorked a wild throw that allowed Suarez to score and make it 2-1. Ke'Bryan Hayes tied the game with a two-out single to center to bring home Bleday. After Busch made it 3-2 in the sixth with his 20th homer, Chicago scored an insurance run in the eighth. Pinch hitter Ian Happ walked with one out and went to second on a wild pitch. Hoerner drove him in with a single past shortstop for a two-run Cubs lead. Swanson's 19th homer gave the Cubs a three-run lead in the ninth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ed Sheeran calls Israel's treatment of Gazans 'unjustifiable,' apologizes for Macklemore controversy
item.description: Pop star Ed Sheeran apologized on Saturday for his handling of a controversy that erupted this week when rapper Macklemore was removed as an opening act over comments on the occupied Palestinian territories.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandra Michalska, Nolan Mccaskill
item.content:encoded: Pop star Ed Sheeran apologized on Saturday for his handling of a controversy that erupted this week when rapper Macklemore was removed as an opening act over comments on the occupied Palestinian territories. Breaking his silence on the issue, the British singer decried Israel's treatment of residents in Gaza as "unjustifiable." "I've had to take and make difficult decisions and I am making mistakes and I'm so, so sorry," Sheeran told an audience in Philadelphia, where he performed for the first time since Macklemore was taken off the concert tour. At the start of the concert at Lincoln Financial Field, Sheeran called the October 2023 Hamas attack that killed 1,200 Israelis "horrific." But he called Israel's subsequent war, which has killed thousands in Gaza and displaced almost all of the population, "catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate." Sheeran also decried "systemic injustice" in the West Bank, where Israel's right-wing coalition government has allowed a massive expansion of Jewish settlements. The pop star's opening statement on Saturday offered a stark change from his statements earlier in the week, when Sheeran posted on Instagram that his concert audiences "do not expect a political forum." Controversy has surrounded Sheeran since [USN:L4N4561KP TEXT:"Macklemore posted on Instagram"] that New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft had told Sheeran that Macklemore would not be allowed to perform at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, where Sheeran has shows on September 25 and 26. Macklemore said Kraft and other stadium owners had told Sheeran he would not be allowed to perform in their venues if Macklemore remained on the tour after saying "Free Palestine" during a September 4 concert at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The tour's other supporting acts [USN:L1N4570ZS TEXT:"subsequently quit"] to show solidarity with Macklemore. Despite acceding to stadium owners' demand for Macklemore's removal, Sheeran on Saturday said he was "deeply worried" about concert venues vetting performers' content. "This happens in so many places that I perform around the world, but it should never happen in the free world," Sheeran said. The controversy, however, did not matter to people who spoke to Reuters on Saturday before Sheeran took to the stage. Joy VanRuler, a 55-year-old teacher from Pottstown, Pennsylvania, said she supports both artists. "It doesn't need to be political," VanRuler said in an interview outside the stadium in Philadelphia. "It's about the music, and we support both of them and it's all good." Macklemore "shouldn't have talked about politics," said Javier Hernandez, a 62-year-old designer from Allentown, Pennsylvania, whose daughter invited him to the concert. "It gives the people an opportunity to raise their voices and just make a mess of the whole situation. He should have just left it alone." Dozens of pro-Palestinian protesters gathered about half a mile from the concert venue ahead of Sheeran's performance. Organizers said they were there to talk to people about the conditions on the ground in Gaza and to highlight local groups advocating for Palestinians.

item.title: China keeps benchmark lending rates unchanged for 16th month in September
item.description: China kept its benchmark lending rates unchanged for the 16th straight month on Sunday, in line with market expectations.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China kept its benchmark lending rates unchanged for the 16th straight month on Sunday, in line with market expectations. WHY IT'S IMPORTANT The steady loan prime rates underscored the limited scope for fresh monetary easing after some major [USN:L6N4590JA TEXT:"global central banks"] recently adopted a more hawkish stance, even as the yuan continued to strengthen. BY THE NUMBERS The one-year LPR was kept at 3.00%, while the five-year LPR was unchanged at 3.50%. All 21 market participants in a Reuters [USN:L4N4590N3 TEXT:"survey"] forecast no change to either rate. CONTEXT The Federal Reserve [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"raised"] interest rates last week and flagged more hikes in the coming months, with new US central bank chief Kevin Warsh joining a unanimous decision that effectively acknowledges the Trump administration's inability so far to control inflation that policymakers worry could worsen. The yield premium on benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasuries over Chinese government bonds hovered near the highest level on record after the Fed rate hike. China's slower [USN:ZUN00FCGZ TEXT:"loan growth"] is becoming the new normal as shrinking property and local government sectors sap credit demand faster than emerging industries can fill the gap, central bank Governor Pan Gongsheng [USN:L1N45802L TEXT:"said"]. KEY QUOTES ** Serena Zhou, senior China strategist, Mizuho Securities "Unless domestic demand weakens a lot more materially, the likelihood of broad-based monetary easing in Q4 has diminished in our view, particularly against the backdrop of a more hawkish US Federal Reserve." ** Jacqueline Rong, chief China economist, BNP Paribas "On monetary policy, we believe that China is in the late stage of its rate-cutting cycle. Our base case remains that the People's Bank of China will stay on hold for the rest of this year, constrained by tight net interest margins of banks and a transition from deflation to mild inflation. The risk to our view is tilted to a cut if economic growth disappoints."

item.title: Estadounidense Jovic conquista el Abierto de Guadalajara en México por segunda ocasión
item.description: La estadounidense Iva Jovic, número 16 del mundo, conquistó el sábado el Abierto de Guadalajara por segunda ocasión consecutiva tras vencer por 6-4 y 6-2 a la también estadounidense Peyton Stearns en la final del torneo de tenis categoría 500 que se disputó en canchas de superficie dura en el occidente de México.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La estadounidense Iva Jovic, número 16 del mundo, conquistó el sábado el Abierto de Guadalajara por segunda ocasión consecutiva tras vencer por 6-4 y 6-2 a la también estadounidense Peyton Stearns en la final del torneo de tenis categoría 500 que se disputó en canchas de superficie dura en el occidente de México. Con su triunfo, la jugadora de 18 años subirá dos lugares en la clasificación de la WTA. En el primer set, ambas jugadoras mantuvieron sus servicios en los primeros ocho juegos, pero Jovic quebró el servicio de su oponente para ponerse 5-4 y ganó el set cuando Stearns falló en su devolución por cuarta ocasión. En el segundo set, Jovic lo inició quebrándole el servicio a su rival que se empezó a ver desconcertada fallando la mayoría de sus devoluciones, y confirmó su quiebre cuando Stearns mandó su devolución a la red. Stearns, número 60 de la WTA, comenzó a reaccionar y puso el set 3-2, pero Jovic, con sus potentes y colocados servicios, ganó el sexto juego. En el séptimo juego, Stearns cometió dobles faltas y falló en sus devoluciones, lo que permitió que Jovic le quebrara su servicio cuando Stearns mandó la pelota a la red. Jovic logró el bicampeonato con una colocada devolución de revés paralela en un juego que duró una hora y 26 minutos. En su camino al bicampeonato, Jovic no perdió ningún set y, además de Stearns, venció a la turca Zeynep Sonmez, a la polaca Magdalena Frech y a la española Cristina Bucsa.

item.title: NFL mandates matching video displays during kicking attempts
item.description: The NFL has informed clubs that stadium video displays must be the same for both the home and visiting team while kickers are attempting field goals and extra points, in a move to ensure competitive equity.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The NFL has informed clubs that stadium video displays must be the same for both the home and visiting team while kickers are attempting field goals and extra points, in a move to ensure competitive equity. Prior to the rule change that was outlined in a memo sent to teams last week and obtained by Reuters on Saturday, all video and ribbon boards only had to display either a static image or an All-22 view that showed every player on the field at one time. But now the same All-22 angle or static image must be used for both kicking teams. "To ensure competitive equity, clubs must apply this requirement consistently and use the same All-22 angle or static image for both kicking teams," the memo dated September 7 said. "Violations will result in accountability measures." The NFL did not explain why the rule was changed ahead of the 2026 season and would not say if it was connected to a September 1 social media post by former analytics coach Ryan Paganetti. In the post, Paganetti said that after going through more than a decade of New England Patriots broadcasts, he noticed that when opposing kickers lined up at Gillette Stadium, the video board showed a reverse view of the kick. The result, according to Paganetti, was that the video board placed "a second, offset set of yellow uprights directly behind the real ones" that created a visual distortion for the kickers. Paganetti, who worked for the Philadelphia Eagles, Jacksonville Jaguars and Las Vegas Raiders, added that of the 52 Patriots field goal attempts he reviewed, the reverse angle was never displayed on the video board. The Patriots did not immediately reply when asked by Reuters for comment.

item.title: Apple's Tim Cook sees Australia's social media curbs as 'world-leading', PM says
item.description: Apple Executive Chair Tim Cook views the Australian government's pioneering curbs on social media as "world-leading", Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Sunday after meeting with Cook at the company's US headquarters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Apple Executive Chair Tim Cook views the Australian government's pioneering curbs on social media as "world-leading", Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Sunday after meeting with Cook at the company's US headquarters. "Tim Cook gave us a lot of time this morning. He regards the work that we’ve done on social media to be world-leading," Albanese said in remarks from Apple Park, California, televised in Australia on Sunday. Australia this month took the [USN:L1N45003L TEXT:"next step"] in its push to improve online safety with a plan to give social media users the option to select the content they see on their feeds. In December Australia became the first country to ban social media for children under 16. Other governments have followed this year, with the European Commission the latest to propose such a ban for children under 13. Asked for comment on Albanese's remarks, an Apple spokesperson referred to a post by Cook on X, saying he was grateful to share with Albanese "some of our newest innovations, including strong and intuitive controls to help keep kids safe online". Cook recently [USN:L4N44T1T0 TEXT:"stepped down"] as Apple (AAPL.O) CEO after 15 years in the role. Albanese's visit to the US comes as industry leaders there are [USN:L1N4590AS TEXT:"split"] over how fast companies should develop the increasingly powerful technology, and as an AI [USN:L6N4590A6 TEXT:"safety debate"] roils Silicon Valley. Albanese said AI entails risks that must be mitigated. "There is a need for a discussion about what the global framework is for the roll out of AI, because it is moving very quickly, and we need to make sure that humans remain in control," he told reporters, according to an official transcript. The Australian leader's comments contrast with the position of President Donald Trump, who has [USN:L1N4560HH TEXT:"downplayed concerns"] about AI and argued that additional regulation is unnecessary.

item.title: Saudi drop Al Juwayr from Gulf Cup squad over 'disciplinary' issue
item.description: Musab Al Juwayr has been dropped from hosts Saudi Arabia's squad for the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup due to unspecified "disciplinary reasons", the national team said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Musab Al Juwayr has been dropped from hosts Saudi Arabia's squad for the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup due to unspecified "disciplinary reasons", the national team said on Saturday. "The national team's technical and administrative staff have decided to exclude player Musab Al Juwayr from the Green Falcons' training camp in Jeddah in preparation for Gulf Cup 27 due to disciplinary reasons," the Saudi national team posted on X. The team did not provide further details on the disciplinary issue and said a replacement would be named later. The 23-year-old Al Qadsiah playmaker had been included in the 26-man squad announced by Greek coach Georgios Donis earlier in the week for the tournament. The former Al Hilal and Al Shabab player, who was part of Saudi Arabia's World Cup squad this summer, has earned 39 caps and scored 6 goals for his country. Saudi Arabia open their campaign against Kuwait next Wednesday before taking on Oman and Iraq in Group A. The tournament will be held in Saudi Arabia from Wednesday to October 6.

item.title: Independiente remonta y gana en liga argentina; cae River Plate
item.description: Independiente de Avellaneda remontó un marcador adverso y venció el sábado por 2-1 en su visita a Unión de Santa Fe, en una jornada en la cual River Plate perdió por 2-1 ante Huracán.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Independiente de Avellaneda remontó un marcador adverso y venció el sábado por 2-1 en su visita a Unión de Santa Fe, en una jornada en la cual River Plate perdió por 2-1 ante Huracán. Con la victoria, Independiente llegó a 17 puntos y subió al quinto lugar de la tabla de posiciones de la Zona A que lidera Instituto de Córdoba con 19. "Fue un triunfo con carácter, fútbol, preparación física y con un plantel que está comprometido. El equipo manejó prácticamente todo el partido", dijo el director técnico uruguayo Jadson Viera en conferencia de prensa. En el partido disputado en el estadio 15 de abril de la ciudad de Santa Fe, Unión abrió el marcador a los 49 minutos por intermedio del paraguayo Marcelo Estigarribia. El popular conjunto argentino remontó con goles de Santiago Montiel y Maximiliano Meza a los 51 y 57 minutos, respectivamente. Por su parte, River Plate perdió por 2-1 como local ante Huracán e interrumpió una racha de tres victorias seguidas en la liga argentina desde el debut del director técnico Leonardo Ponzio. "Perdimos un partido en el que fuimos para adelante y generamos situaciones. Dos pelotas de mierda nos convierten y el resultado tira abajo todo lo que hicimos", dijo Nicolás Otamendi tras la derrota. En el encuentro en el estadio Monumental, Huracán abrió el marcador al minuto nueve con un tiro libre del colombiano Óscar Cortés que sorprendió al portero Santiago Beltrán. En la segunda parte, River Plate igualó a los 65 minutos con un remate de larga distancia de Tomás Galván, mientras que Huracán volvió a sacar ventaja a los 80 por intermedio de Lucas Blondel. "Sabíamos que veníamos a uno de los estadios más complicados. No tuvimos mucho la pelota, pero a veces hay que ganar como sea, y Blondel nos regaló el segundo gol", dijo el portero de Huracán, Hernán Galíndez, a la televisión local. En otros partidos del sábado, Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata y Banfield igualaron por 2-2, mientras que Gimnasia y Esgrima de Mendoza y Deportivo Riestra empataron sin goles. El viernes, Racing Club sacó su segundo triunfo en el torneo al vencer por 3-1 a Sarmiento, en tanto que Central Córdoba y Defensa y Justicia igualaron por 2-2.

item.title: US says it killed four in strike on vessel in the Caribbean
item.description: The US military said it killed four people in a strike on a vessel in the Caribbean on Saturday that it alleged was involved in drug trafficking.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US military said it killed four people in a strike on a vessel in the Caribbean on Saturday that it alleged was involved in drug trafficking. "Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel's active involvement in narco-trafficking," the military's Southern Command posted on X. The attack was the latest in a campaign dating back to last year that targets what the Trump administration describes as "narco-terrorists." Saturday's announcement comes 10 days after a strike, also in the Caribbean, that killed three people, the US military said. Since the campaign started, US strikes on vessels in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific have killed more than 220 people. Rights groups have labeled the attacks "extrajudicial killings."

item.title: Francisco Alvarez's blast ignites Mets rout of Phillies
item.description: Francisco Alvarez had two hits Saturday, including the go-ahead three-run homer in the fifth, as the host New York Mets routed the skidding Philadelphia Phillies 10-3.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Francisco Alvarez had two hits Saturday, including the go-ahead three-run homer in the fifth, as the host New York Mets routed the skidding Philadelphia Phillies 10-3. Carson Benge was 3-for-4 with a solo homer and two RBIs for the Mets (71-84), who have won the middle two games of the four-game series. Brett Baty had two hits, including a run-scoring single, while Benge, Juan Soto and Bo Bichette each had RBI singles during a four-run eighth. Ronny Mauricio and Francisco Lindor worked bases-loaded walks. Jefry Yan (2-1), the first of five Mets relievers, earned the win by allowing two hits over 1 1/3 innings. Cionel Perez, Jonathan Pintaro, Dedniel Nunez and Tobias Myers combined to blank the Phillies on one hit over the final three innings. Mets starter Christian Scott allowed three runs on six hits and one walk while striking out seven over 4 2/3 innings. Alec Bohm had RBI singles in the fourth and fifth for the Phillies (85-70), who missed a chance to take over the top National League wild card, at least temporarily. The Chicago Cubs (86-69) and San Diego Padres (86-69) both won to remain tied atop the NL wild-card race. Bryce Harper had a double and sacrifice fly while Trea Turner and Luis Arraez added two hits apiece for the Phillies, who fell to 7-10 in September. Andrew Painter (3-10) took the loss after surrendering four runs on four hits and one walk while striking out six over 5 1/3 innings. Benge homered leading off the second. Bohm tied the score in the fourth before the Phillies chased Scott in the fifth when Harper lofted a tie-breaking sacrifice fly before Bohm's RBI single to left off Yan. The Mets took the lead in a 10-pitch span against Painter leading off the bottom of the inning. Marcus Semien drew a four-pitch walk and Baty singled before Alvarez hit a 387-foot opposite field homer to right. Mauricio drew a bases-loaded walk in the sixth, as did Lindor in the eighth before the consecutive RBI singles by Soto, Bichette and Benge. --Field Level Media
